task_description:
Objective: Build a rigorous, cross-article synthesis of urban heat island (UHI) mitigation strategies using Wikipedia tools only. Produce a structured report that identifies key strategies, compares coverage across multiple primary articles, highlights commonly linked topics, and surfaces frequently related topics. Include validation checks and iterative refinement where specified.

Concrete queries, thresholds, and workflow:
1) Seed discovery (sequential; may branch to expansion):
   - Use Wikipedia:search_wikipedia with query="urban heat island mitigation strategies" and limit=20 to obtain candidate article titles.
   - For each returned title, call Wikipedia:get_summary and retain those whose TITLE or SUMMARY contains at least one of these keywords (case-insensitive): ["urban heat island", "UHI", "mitigation", "cool roof", "green roof", "albedo", "tree canopy", "urban forestry", "heat"].
   - If fewer than 5 titles pass this filter, perform the following additional searches (each with limit=10), merge all results, and deduplicate by exact title:
       a) query="urban heat island"
       b) query="cool roof"
       c) query="green roof"
       d) query="urban forestry"
       e) query="reflective pavement"
       f) query="heat wave mitigation"
     Re-apply the same keyword filter on titles/summaries. If still fewer than 5 pass, keep all passing results (even if <5) and proceed; otherwise, select the top 5–8 filtered titles (max 8), prioritizing titles whose summaries mention both a UHI-related term ("urban heat island" or "UHI") and an intervention term ("mitigation", "strategy", "measure").

2) Section-driven extraction (sequential per article; decision-based):
   - For each selected primary article (5–8 total), call Wikipedia:get_sections.
   - Identify section titles that match any of these section keywords (case-insensitive substring match): ["Mitigation", "Prevention", "Reducing", "Reduction", "Strategies", "Countermeasures", "Adaptation", "Measures", "Policy"]. Let these be the mitigation-related sections.
   - For each mitigation-related section found, call Wikipedia:summarize_article_section with max_length=180. If no mitigation-related sections are found for an article, call Wikipedia:summarize_article_for_query with query="mitigation strategies for urban heat island or reducing urban heat" and max_length=250 for that article.

3) Key facts extraction (sequential per article):
   - For each selected primary article, call Wikipedia:extract_key_facts with topic_within_article="mitigation strategies; interventions; effectiveness; cost; implementation barriers" and count=7. This will be used to structure per-article bullet points of strategies and qualitative/quantitative insights.

4) Link overlap analysis (requires prior completion of Step 2/3 for all articles; combined/parallel):
   - For each selected primary article, call Wikipedia:get_links.
   - Compute overlap across all selected primary articles: collect the set of linked page titles that appear in at least 3 different primary articles (overlap threshold=3). Choose up to 5 overlapping linked titles (if more than 5, choose the 5 with highest frequency of appearance across articles; break ties by alphabetical order).
   - For each chosen overlapping link title, call Wikipedia:get_summary and Wikipedia:extract_key_facts with count=3 (topic_within_article="UHI mitigation relevance"), to provide concise context and salient points for why these links are commonly referenced.

5) Related topics frequency (parallel per article, then combine):
   - For each selected primary article, call Wikipedia:get_related_topics with limit=15.
   - Aggregate all related topics across the primary articles, compute frequency, and select the top 5 topics by frequency that are not already among the primary articles or the overlapping links selected in Step 4. For each of these 5 frequent related topics, call Wikipedia:get_summary to include short contextual descriptions.

6) Deep cross-validation (iterative, decision-based):
   - Identify the 2 primary articles with the highest count of mitigation-related sections (from Step 2). If tied, choose the two with the greatest number of extracted key facts mentioning at least one of the following keywords in the fact text: ["albedo", "vegetation", "roof", "pavement", "tree", "shade", "cooling", "reflective"].
   - For these two articles, call Wikipedia:get_article to retrieve the full content.
   - Validation check: For each of the 7 key facts extracted in Step 3 for those two articles, verify whether the main noun phrases or distinctive terms in the fact (e.g., "cool roofs", "green roofs", "urban forestry", "reflective pavements", "albedo increase") appear verbatim or as close variants in the full article text. If more than 30% of the facts for a given article are not corroborated by the full text (i.e., fewer than 5 of the 7 facts can be matched by searching the full text for their key terms), re-run Wikipedia:extract_key_facts for that article with count=5 (same topic_within_article), and use this revised set for the final report for that article.

7) Final report requirements (structured, self-contained output using only tool-derived data):
   - Section A: Primary Articles Used
     • List 5–8 chosen primary article titles. For each, include a one-sentence description (from its summary) and indicate which path was used: "section-based" (summarize_article_section was used) or "query-based" (summarize_article_for_query fallback).
   - Section B: Per-Article Mitigation Highlights
     • For each primary article: list the mitigation-related section titles used (if any) and include 2–4 concise bullets synthesizing the section summaries and the extracted key facts (prioritize facts that match the validation criteria if Step 6 applied). Each bullet should end with a simple provenance tag like [Article: <title>; Section: <section title> or Query].
   - Section C: Cross-Article Comparison
     • List common mitigation strategies (those appearing in at least 3 primary articles by name or clear synonym) and unique strategies (appearing in only 1 article), with 1–2 lines each summarizing their gist and any noted effectiveness/limitations.
   - Section D: Overlapping Linked Topics (from Step 4)
     • List up to 5 overlapping link titles, each with a 1–2 sentence summary and 1–2 key facts (from the 3 extracted), explaining their relevance to UHI mitigation (e.g., mechanisms, materials, urban design elements).
   - Section E: Frequently Related Topics (from Step 5)
     • List the 5 most frequent related topics (not already covered in Section D), each with a brief summary and a one-line note on how it expands the mitigation landscape.
   - Section F: Method and Decision Notes
     • Document the number of articles considered vs. selected, which additional queries were used (if any), the number of mitigation-related sections found per article, and the validation outcome for the two deep-validated articles (including whether re-extraction was triggered and why).

Execution constraints and notes:
- All steps must be executed using the specified Wikipedia tools only; do not use external resources.
- All keyword checks and thresholds are explicitly provided; follow them exactly.
- Keep numeric thresholds: primary articles selected=5–8; overlap threshold=3; overlapping links capped at 5; related topics selected=5; key facts per primary article initially=7; re-extraction facts count=5.
- Ensure every tool listed is used at least once as prescribed by the workflow.
- The report should be plain text with clear sections and bullet lists as described; avoid heavy formatting.
dependency_analysis:
Inherent tool dependencies and natural workflows:
- search_wikipedia → (titles) → get_summary/get_sections/get_links/get_related_topics/get_article/extract_key_facts/summarize_article_section: Searching yields candidate article titles that feed all subsequent tools. This is the primary discovery mechanism.
- get_sections → summarize_article_section: Section titles are needed to target mitigation-relevant portions; the section summary tool requires a valid section_title, so discovery of sections precedes summarization.
- summarize_article_for_query: Fallback summarization depends on the article title and a targeted query string when no relevant sections are found.
- extract_key_facts: Consumes the article title and an optional topical focus; its output is later cross-validated against full article text from get_article.
- get_links: Produces linked page titles used to compute overlap across articles; these link titles then become inputs to get_summary and extract_key_facts for contextual expansion.
- get_related_topics: Produces semantically related topics used to identify frequently co-related subjects across articles; chosen topics then feed into get_summary for concise context.
- get_article: Provides full content for validation against previously extracted key facts, enabling iterative refinement by potentially re-running extract_key_facts.

Scenario-based dependencies and decision points:
- Branching after search: If fewer than 5 articles pass the keyword filter (based on get_summary outputs), the workflow triggers additional search_wikipedia calls with pre-specified queries. This conditionally expands the candidate set and forces deduplication and re-filtering.
- Section-based vs. query-based summarization: get_sections determines whether summarize_article_section is viable. If no section matches mitigation-related keywords, the workflow switches to summarize_article_for_query with a precise query string.
- Overlap-driven expansion: get_links results from all selected articles are aggregated; only links that appear in at least 3 different articles are retained. These overlapping link titles then trigger parallel calls to get_summary and extract_key_facts, enriching the cross-article context.
- Frequency-based topic selection: get_related_topics outputs are combined and tallied. The top 5 frequent topics not already covered become inputs for get_summary. This step depends on previously selected primary articles and ensures diversity of covered topics.
- Iterative validation loop: For two key articles (selected based on mitigation-related section counts and content cues in extracted facts), get_article provides full text. A comparison step checks whether extracted key facts are corroborated by the full text. If more than 30% are not corroborated, extract_key_facts is re-run with adjusted count (5), and the revised set supersedes the earlier facts. This introduces an iterative corrective mechanism.

Parallel vs. sequential requirements:
- Sequential phases: Discovery (search_wikipedia → get_summary filter), Section discovery (get_sections), and validation (get_article) are sequential and gate later steps.
- Parallelizable phases: After primary articles are selected, per-article calls to get_sections, summarize_article_section or summarize_article_for_query, extract_key_facts, and get_links can proceed in parallel across articles. However, link overlap computation requires that all get_links calls complete before choosing overlapping links and issuing further calls on them. Similarly, related topics frequency analysis requires all get_related_topics calls to complete before selecting the top 5.

Cross-server considerations:
- All tools are on the Wikipedia server for this task; there are no cross-server dependencies. All data acquisition, summarization, fact extraction, section and link handling, and validation occur within this single server environment.

Critical data flow patterns:
- Titles cascade: search_wikipedia → titles → (get_summary for filtering) → selected titles → (get_sections) → section titles → summarize_article_section.
- Fallback path: If get_sections yields no relevant sections → summarize_article_for_query with a predefined, mitigation-specific query.
- Validation loop: extract_key_facts → (if selected for deep validation) get_article → corroboration check → conditional re-run of extract_key_facts with adjusted count.
- Expansion via connections: get_links across articles → overlap filtering → per-link get_summary + extract_key_facts; get_related_topics across articles → frequency tally → per-topic get_summary.

These dependencies enforce understanding of how each tool’s outputs set parameters or determine the use of subsequent tools, mandate conditional branching and iterative refinement, and require combining parallel results into later selection-dependent steps.

task_description:
Over the upcoming week, our historical research team needs a highly structured comparative analysis of three defining expeditions of the Heroic Age of Antarctic Exploration. Execute the following research workflow using the Wikipedia tools provided:

1. Initial Discovery: Use `search_wikipedia` to locate the main article for the 'Heroic Age of Antarctic Exploration'.

2. Expedition Targeting: From your knowledge or by scanning the main article, identify the exact Wikipedia article titles for these three specific expeditions: Roald Amundsen's South Pole expedition, Robert Falcon Scott's Terra Nova Expedition, and Ernest Shackleton's Imperial Trans-Antarctic Expedition.

3. Section-Based Extraction: For EACH of the three expedition articles:
   a) Use `get_sections` to retrieve the article's structure.
   b) Identify the specific section discussing the 'Preparations', 'Ships', or 'Equipment' (select the most relevant one based on the section list).
   c) Use `summarize_article_section` (max_length: 200) on that specific section to determine the primary vessel used.
   d) Identify the section detailing the 'Journey', 'Expedition', or 'Arrival at the pole'. Use `summarize_article_section` (max_length: 250) to summarize the core journey.

4. Conditional Fact Extraction: For EACH expedition article, use `extract_key_facts` (count: 4) focused specifically on the topic 'fate of the crew and the leader'.
   - If the key facts indicate the leader survived the expedition (like Amundsen and Shackleton), proceed to Step 5.
   - If the key facts indicate the leader died during the expedition (like Scott), use `summarize_article_for_query` on the expedition article to extract details about 'search party and discovery of the final camp'.

5. Biographical Deep Dive: For the leaders who survived their respective Antarctic expeditions, search for their main biographical Wikipedia articles ('Roald Amundsen' and 'Ernest Shackleton'). Use `summarize_article_for_query` (max_length: 200) on their biographical articles with the query 'final expedition and cause of death' to determine how they ultimately died in their later years.

6. Final Synthesis: Compile your findings into a comprehensive markdown report titled 'Comparative Analysis of Antarctic Expeditions'. The report must include a dedicated section for each expedition detailing the vessel used, the journey summary, the immediate fate of the crew, and the ultimate historical fate/cause of death of the leader.
dependency_analysis:
This task features a deep, multi-stage dependency chain utilizing almost the entire suite of Wikipedia tools. 

1. Sequential Dependency: `search_wikipedia` is required to establish the precise article titles for the expeditions, which act as the required 'title' input for all subsequent operations.
2. Iterative & Transformative Flow: The agent must use `get_sections` on three separate articles. The output (a list of sections) must be parsed by the agent to make a decision on which exact string to pass as the 'section_title' parameter into `summarize_article_section`. This prevents the agent from guessing section headers, which often vary across Wikipedia articles.
3. Conditional Branching: The workflow requires `extract_key_facts` to evaluate the immediate survival of the expedition leaders. The output data dictates the next tool execution: if the leader died during the expedition (Scott), the workflow branches to investigate the search party via `summarize_article_for_query` on the expedition article. If they survived, it branches to cross-article research, requiring the agent to navigate to the leaders' biographical pages to find their ultimate causes of death.
4. Parameter Constraint Enforcement: The agent must respect specific `max_length` and `count` parameters mapped to different phases of the investigation, demonstrating control over tool schema properties.

task_description:
Research synthesis task: Build a structured, evidence-based brief on traditional Polynesian navigation and the broader Austronesian expansion, combining multiple Wikipedia articles, section-targeted summaries, key fact extraction, cross-topic network analysis, and controversy assessment. The goal is to identify core navigational techniques, construct a chronology of settlement, evaluate debated pre-Columbian contacts, summarize modern revivals, and analyze related-topic overlap. Use only the provided Wikipedia tools. Follow the steps and decision logic below, and produce the final output in the specified structure.

Primary target article titles to resolve and analyze:
- Polynesian navigation
- Micronesian navigation
- Stick charts
- Austronesian expansion
- Lapita culture
- Hōkūleʻa
- Pre-Columbian trans-oceanic contact

Phase 0 – Title resolution (ensures consistent titles for subsequent calls):
1) For each target string above, resolve the exact article title to use. Do this in two steps per item:
   a. Call Wikipedia:search_wikipedia with the target string (use limit = 10). If a result exactly matches the target string (case-insensitive), select that title. If not, select the closest obvious match in the results (for example, for "Hōkūleʻa" search with query "Hokulea" as well if needed and select the diacritics version if present). Record a mapping of requested_string → resolved_title.
   b. Call Wikipedia:get_article with the resolved_title. If this call fails, retry Wikipedia:search_wikipedia with a simplified query (e.g., remove diacritics or use a well-known synonym: for Hōkūleʻa use "Hokulea"; for Pre-Columbian trans-oceanic contact use "Pre-Columbian transoceanic contact"), then select the top sensible result and proceed. Update the mapping accordingly.
   c. For each resolved_title, also call Wikipedia:get_summary to store a quick-reference summary.

Phase 1 – Techniques extraction (Polynesian and Micronesian traditions + tools):
2) For each of the resolved titles among {Polynesian navigation, Micronesian navigation, Stick charts}:
   a. Call Wikipedia:get_sections to retrieve section titles.
   b. Decision: If any section title contains one of these case-insensitive keywords: ["Technique", "Method", "Practice", "Principle", "Navigational", "Tool"], then for each matching section call Wikipedia:summarize_article_section with max_length = 300. If no matching section exists, call Wikipedia:summarize_article_for_query with query = "navigational techniques and tools used (stars, swells, birds, clouds, stick charts)" and max_length = 300.
   c. Call Wikipedia:extract_key_facts with topic_within_article = "techniques" and count = 7.
   d. From the combined summaries and key facts across these three articles, compile a deduplicated list of at least 5 distinct techniques (examples to look for include but are not limited to: star paths, swell pattern reading, bird flight cues, cloud/reflection cues, dead reckoning, stick charts). For each technique, keep a short definition (1–2 sentences) and enumerate which article(s) it was derived from.

Phase 2 – Chronology of settlement (Austronesian expansion + Lapita culture):
3) For each of the resolved titles among {Austronesian expansion, Lapita culture}:
   a. Call Wikipedia:get_sections.
   b. Decision: If any section title contains one of ["Chronology", "Timeline", "Migration", "Expansion", "Settlement"], summarize each such section with Wikipedia:summarize_article_section (max_length = 350). If none match, call Wikipedia:summarize_article_for_query with query = "chronology of expansion and settlement including approximate date ranges and regions" and max_length = 350.
   c. Call Wikipedia:extract_key_facts with topic_within_article = "chronology" and count = 10.
   d. Synthesize at least 7 chronological anchor points, each with an approximate date or range and a region/location (e.g., island groups or oceanic regions), citing which article each point came from.

Phase 3 – Controversies assessment (pre-Columbian contacts debate):
4) For each of {Pre-Columbian trans-oceanic contact, Polynesian navigation}:
   a. Call Wikipedia:get_sections.
   b. Decision: If a section exists with one of ["Polynesian contact", "Evidence", "Americas", "Controversy", "Debate"], summarize those sections with Wikipedia:summarize_article_section (max_length = 300). Otherwise, call Wikipedia:summarize_article_for_query with query = "Polynesian contact with the Americas; evidence such as sweet potato (kumara), chickens, DNA, linguistic" and max_length = 300.
   c. Call Wikipedia:extract_key_facts with topic_within_article = "Polynesian contact" and count = 7.
5) From the combined results, scan for the presence of at least two of these keywords across the two articles: ["sweet potato", "kumara", "chicken", "DNA", "genetic", "linguistic", "Mapuche"]. Decision:
   - If at least two keywords appear in total across the two articles' summaries or extracted facts, classify the statement "Pre-Columbian Polynesian contact with the Americas" as "disputed with multiple lines of evidence" and list 2–3 concise evidence bullets with the source article names.
   - Otherwise, classify the statement as "insufficient evidence in surveyed articles" and list whichever single line (if any) was found.
   In either case, ensure at least 2 controversy items are listed (e.g., one on sweet potato transport, another on possible chicken remains or DNA/linguistics), each with a short description and source titles.

Phase 4 – Modern revival and validation (Hōkūleʻa):
6) For Hōkūleʻa (resolved_title identified in Phase 0):
   a. Call Wikipedia:get_sections.
   b. Decision: If sections include ["Voyages", "History", "Legacy"] (any that exist), summarize each with Wikipedia:summarize_article_section (max_length = 300). If none of these exist, call Wikipedia:summarize_article_for_query with query = "major voyages, achievements, and cultural significance of Hōkūleʻa" and max_length = 300.
   c. Call Wikipedia:extract_key_facts with topic_within_article = "voyages" and count = 5.
   d. Produce at least 3 achievements with years and brief significance statements.

Phase 5 – Cross-topic network analysis (overlap and uniqueness):
7) For each of {Polynesian navigation, Micronesian navigation, Austronesian expansion}:
   a. Call Wikipedia:get_related_topics with limit = 20.
   b. Compute the intersection across the three returned topic lists. Decision:
      - If the intersection size is fewer than 3 topics, re-run Wikipedia:get_related_topics for each with limit = 30 and recompute.
   c. Produce:
      - Shared topics: 3–5 topics present in all three lists (after limit expansion if performed).
      - Unique topics: at least 2 topics uniquely associated with each of the three articles (present in one list but not the others).

Phase 6 – Link validation (internal linking evidence of relationships):
8) Call Wikipedia:get_links for each of {Polynesian navigation, Hōkūleʻa}.
   a. Check whether the resolved titles for {Micronesian navigation, Stick charts} appear in the "Polynesian navigation" link list; record each as present or not present.
   b. Check whether the resolved titles for {Polynesian navigation, Micronesian navigation} appear in the "Hōkūleʻa" link list; record each as present or not present.
   If any expected links are missing, note this in a brief comment in the final output (e.g., "Micronesian navigation not directly linked from Hōkūleʻa"), otherwise confirm linkage.

Final output format (produce a single structured JSON object with these top-level keys):
- sources_used: list of objects [{requested_string, resolved_title, summary}], one per primary target, where "summary" is the output of Wikipedia:get_summary for that title.
- techniques: list of objects [{name, description, sources: [resolved_title,...]}] with at least 5 techniques.
- chronology: list of objects [{approx_date_or_range, region_or_location, source_title}] with at least 7 entries.
- controversies: list of at least 2 objects [{statement, classification, evidence_keywords_found: [..], evidence_bullets: [..], sources: [resolved_title,..]}].
- modern_revival: object {highlights_summary: string, achievements: [{year_or_range, achievement, significance}], source_title: resolved_title_for_Hōkūleʻa}.
- network_analysis: object {shared_topics: [..], unique_topics: {polynesian_navigation: [..], micronesian_navigation: [..], austronesian_expansion: [..]}, limit_used: 20_or_30}.
- link_validation: object {polynesian_navigation: {checked_for: ["Micronesian navigation", "Stick charts" with resolved titles], present: [..], missing: [..]}, hokulea: {checked_for: ["Polynesian navigation", "Micronesian navigation" with resolved titles], present: [..], missing: [..]}, comments: string}.

Constraints and notes:
- Do not use any external resources beyond the Wikipedia tools provided.
- Preserve and report the exact resolved titles selected after Phase 0; all subsequent calls must use those titles.
- All decision branches described above must be executed as specified (e.g., section-targeted summaries when sections are available; otherwise fall back to query-tailored summaries).
dependency_analysis:
INHERENT DEPENDENCIES AND TOOL CHAINS:
- search_wikipedia → get_article → get_sections → summarize_article_section: Standard discovery pipeline. search_wikipedia identifies candidate titles; get_article confirms retrievability; get_sections exposes section names that drive targeted summaries; summarize_article_section extracts focused content.
- get_article/get_summary provide baseline context used to interpret section summaries and extracted facts.
- summarize_article_for_query is a fallback when no relevant sections exist; it depends on resolved titles and crafted queries from the scenario.
- extract_key_facts depends on a confirmed title and, optionally, a topic focus string (e.g., "techniques", "chronology") that is derived from the scenario’s goals.
- get_related_topics depends on confirmed titles and feeds into a set-intersection/uniqueness analysis that may trigger a second round with expanded limits.
- get_links operates on confirmed titles to validate assumptions about inter-article relationships discovered via related topics and content summaries.

SCENARIO-BASED DEPENDENCIES (DECISION POINTS AND FLOWS):
1) Title resolution loop (Phase 0):
   - For each target string, search_wikipedia is used first to resolve an exact title. That resolved title is then passed to get_article. If get_article fails (e.g., diacritics in "Hōkūleʻa"), the workflow loops back to search_wikipedia with an alternate query ("Hokulea") and retries. The final resolved title is persisted and used for all subsequent calls. get_summary is called to store per-article baseline context.
2) Section-targeted vs. query-targeted summarization (Phases 1–4):
   - get_sections output determines whether summarize_article_section can be used. If section keywords are detected (e.g., Techniques/Methods or Chronology/Timeline), those specific sections are summarized; otherwise, summarize_article_for_query is invoked with a tailored query string (e.g., "navigational techniques and tools"). Thus, summarize_article_for_query is conditionally dependent on the absence of relevant sections.
3) Techniques synthesis across multiple articles (Phase 1):
   - Summaries from summarize_article_section or summarize_article_for_query are combined with extract_key_facts("techniques"). The agent must deduplicate techniques across Polynesian navigation, Micronesian navigation, and Stick charts; this combination step enforces multi-source dependency and synthesis.
4) Chronology construction with fallback (Phase 2):
   - get_sections informs which sections to summarize for Austronesian expansion and Lapita culture. If insufficient, summarize_article_for_query is used. extract_key_facts("chronology") provides discrete facts that the agent must transform into at least seven chronological anchors, each specifying date/range and region.
5) Controversy classification via cross-article keyword presence (Phase 3):
   - Summaries and extracted facts from Pre-Columbian trans-oceanic contact and Polynesian navigation are scanned for evidence keywords (e.g., "sweet potato", "DNA"). If at least two keywords are found across both, the classification switches to "disputed with multiple lines of evidence"; otherwise, it is "insufficient evidence". This decision hinges on content derived from summarize_article_section/summarize_article_for_query/extract_key_facts.
6) Modern revival extraction (Phase 4):
   - For Hōkūleʻa, section presence guides summarize_article_section; otherwise summarize_article_for_query is used. extract_key_facts("voyages") supports enumerating achievements with years. The final output depends on properly resolving the title (diacritics) and leveraging both section and query-based summaries.
7) Network analysis with iterative expansion (Phase 5):
   - get_related_topics is called for three titles with limit = 20. The intersection across the three lists is computed. If fewer than 3 shared topics are found, this triggers a re-run with limit = 30 before recomputation. Thus, the second call to get_related_topics is conditionally dependent on the size of the intersection from the first call.
8) Link validation cross-check (Phase 6):
   - get_links outputs for Polynesian navigation and Hōkūleʻa are used to verify whether specific resolved titles (Micronesian navigation, Stick charts, Polynesian navigation) are internally linked. This cross-validates associations suggested by get_related_topics and content analysis. Missing links prompt a note in the final output.

PARALLEL VS. SEQUENTIAL ELEMENTS:
- Sequential: Title resolution must precede all other steps for each article. Section-targeted summarization depends on get_sections. Controversy classification depends on completed summaries/facts from both relevant articles. Network analysis must use the final resolved titles.
- Parallel: After titles are resolved, techniques-related articles (Polynesian navigation, Micronesian navigation, Stick charts) can be processed in parallel; likewise for chronology-related articles (Austronesian expansion, Lapita culture). The network analysis across three articles requires all three related-topic lists, which can be fetched in parallel before set operations.

CROSS-SERVER DEPENDENCIES:
- Not applicable. All tools operate within the Wikipedia server. Cross-validation is implemented via cross-article comparisons and link/related-topic checks within the same server.

CRITICAL DATA FLOW HIGHLIGHTS:
- The get_sections outputs act as gatekeepers for choosing summarize_article_section vs summarize_article_for_query.
- The get_related_topics limit parameter is dynamically adjusted based on the computed intersection size.
- Keywords for controversy classification are applied across outputs from multiple articles, requiring aggregation and decision logic.
- Link presence checks (get_links) validate or contradict topical associations inferred from get_related_topics, ensuring robustness of conclusions.

task_description:
Produce a structured policy briefing comparing three invasive species across different regions using only the provided Wikipedia tools. Species and focal regions: (1) Indo-Pacific lionfish invasion in the western Atlantic/Caribbean; (2) Zebra mussel invasion in North America; (3) Brown tree snake invasion on Guam. For each species, you must identify and synthesize: (A) introduction pathways; (B) invaded regions; (C) ecological impacts; (D) economic impacts; (E) control and management strategies. Use the exact tool sequence, decision rules, and queries below. Finally, generate a cross-species comparison highlighting similarities/differences in vectors, impacts, and controls.

Species set and primary search queries (in order):
- Lionfish: ["Invasive lionfish", "Lionfish Atlantic invasion", "Pterois"]
- Zebra mussel: ["Zebra mussel invasive North America", "Zebra mussel invasion", "Zebra mussel"]
- Brown tree snake: ["Brown tree snake Guam", "Guam brown tree snake invasion", "Brown tree snake"]

Section/keyword mapping for targeted categories:
- Introduction pathways: look for section titles containing any of ["Introduction", "Origins", "Origin", "History", "Spread", "Arrival", "Introduction and spread", "Colonization"].
- Invaded regions: look for ["Distribution", "Range", "Geographic distribution", "Global distribution", "Invasive range", "Habitat", "Spread"].
- Ecological impacts: look for ["Ecology", "Environmental impact", "Ecological impact", "Ecosystem effects", "Predation", "Effects on native species"]
- Economic impacts: look for ["Economic impact", "Economic effects", "Cost", "Damage", "Infrastructure impacts"]
- Control/management: look for ["Control", "Management", "Mitigation", "Eradication", "Prevention", "Response", "Countermeasures", "Containment"]

Management method keyword list (to mine from links and summaries): ["control", "management", "eradication", "biocontrol", "biological control", "chemical control", "mechanical", "trapping", "trap", "culling", "poison", "toxin", "fencing", "barrier", "ballast water", "quarantine", "public awareness", "outreach", "regulation", "policy", "prevention", "diver removal", "spearfishing", "bounty", "electric barrier", "rapid response"].

Process (repeat Steps 1–7 for each species separately):
1) Discovery and article selection:
   a. Call Wikipedia:search_wikipedia with the species' first query. If no satisfactory title is found per rule below, try the second query, then the third.
   b. Selection rule: choose the first result whose title contains either the species' common name or scientific name AND (if present) signals an invasion context (strings like "Invasive", "invasion", or specific region like "Guam", "North America"). If none found, choose the species' main article (e.g., "Invasive lionfish" if present; else "Pterois"; "Zebra mussel"; "Brown tree snake"). Record the chosen title.
   c. Call Wikipedia:get_summary for the chosen title to capture a 1–2 sentence overview for the briefing.

2) Section discovery:
   a. Call Wikipedia:get_sections on the chosen title. Keep the full list of section titles.
   b. For each category (Introduction pathways, Invaded regions, Ecological impacts, Economic impacts, Control/management), find the best-matching section title according to the mapping above (case-insensitive contains). If multiple match, pick the one most specific to the invasion context (e.g., if both "Ecology" and "Environmental impact" exist, prefer "Environmental impact"). If none match, mark that category as "no direct section" and proceed to Step 3 with fallback.

3) Targeted summarization per category:
   For each category:
   a. If a matching section was found: call Wikipedia:summarize_article_section with max_length=250 for Introduction pathways, 200 for Invaded regions, 250 for Ecological impacts, 200 for Economic impacts, and 250 for Control/management.
   b. If no matching section: call Wikipedia:summarize_article_for_query with a tailored query string:
      - Introduction pathways: "introduction pathways and how the species arrived to [region]"
      - Invaded regions: "current invaded regions and geographic spread"
      - Ecological impacts: "ecological impacts on native species and ecosystems"
      - Economic impacts: "economic impacts, costs, and infrastructure effects"
      - Control/management: "control and management strategies, prevention, and eradication"
      Use max_length=250 for all fallback summaries.

4) Fact extraction and cross-check:
   a. Call Wikipedia:extract_key_facts twice per species:
      - First with topic_within_article="impact" and count=5 to extract top impact facts (ecological/economic intermingled as available).
      - Second with topic_within_article="control" and count=5 to extract top control/management facts.
   b. Compare the extracted control facts to the Control/management summary from Step 3 to ensure at least one management method appears in both. If not, re-run Wikipedia:summarize_article_for_query with query "detailed control methods and implementation examples" and update the control/management note accordingly.

5) Link mining for management approaches:
   a. Call Wikipedia:get_links for the chosen title.
   b. Filter link titles by the management method keyword list (case-insensitive contains). From the filtered set, select up to 5 unique approach names most directly describing methods (e.g., "Biological control", "Ballast water management", "Trapping", "Culling", "Public awareness campaigns"). If fewer than 3 are found, broaden by including links that contain "Invasive species management" or the species name coupled with a method if present.

6) Related topics validation:
   a. Call Wikipedia:get_related_topics with limit=15 for the chosen title.
   b. Check whether the related topics include any general management or vector topics that corroborate your findings (e.g., "Invasive species", "Biological control", "Ballast water" for zebra mussel; "Overland cargo", "Guam" for brown tree snake; "Spearfishing", "Reef ecology" for lionfish). If a corroborating topic is found, note it. If none are found but Step 4 and Step 5 produced results, proceed; otherwise, return to Step 3 to re-summarize the Control/management and Introduction pathways categories with more specific queries (e.g., include the region name explicitly: "... in the Caribbean", "... in North America", "... on Guam").

7) Fallback for sparse or generic pages:
   If Step 2 found zero matching sections across all categories for a species, call Wikipedia:get_article and then re-run Step 3 entirely using only summarize_article_for_query for all categories. Proceed to Steps 4–6 afterwards.

Final deliverable format (plain text, no tables):
- Title: "Comparative Policy Briefing: Invasive Lionfish (Western Atlantic/Caribbean), Zebra Mussel (North America), and Brown Tree Snake (Guam)"
- For each species, provide:
  1) One-line overview (from get_summary)
  2) Introduction pathways (2–3 sentences)
  3) Invaded regions (bullet list of up to 5 regions)
  4) Ecological impacts (3 bullet points)
  5) Economic impacts (2 bullet points)
  6) Control/management strategies (up to 5 bullet points), clearly indicating at least one method confirmed both by extracted facts and by link mining
  7) Noted corroborating related topic(s) (1–2 items) from get_related_topics
- Cross-species comparison section:
  - Vectors: concise comparison highlighting similarities/differences
  - Impacts: contrast the most severe ecological and economic effects
  - Controls: summarize which strategies appear most consistently effective and under what conditions
  - Gaps/uncertainties: note any category where only fallback summaries were used or corroboration was weak

Execution constraints:
- Use the specified queries in order; only proceed to fallbacks when rules indicate.
- Limit each category summary to the specified max lengths in Step 3.
- Management approaches list must be derived from both extract_key_facts and get_links, with validation via get_related_topics wherever possible.
- Do not use any data source other than the provided Wikipedia tools.
dependency_analysis:
This task relies on a single server (Wikipedia) but requires extensive cross-tool dependencies and iterative branching:

Inherent tool chains:
- search_wikipedia → get_summary/get_sections: The search results determine the exact article title to use for all subsequent calls. get_summary provides a one-line baseline for context; get_sections exposes the article's structure for targeted extraction.
- get_sections → summarize_article_section: Section titles discovered by get_sections directly feed into summarize_article_section for narrowly scoped summaries.
- Section absence → summarize_article_for_query: If no appropriate section exists, the flow branches to summarize_article_for_query with category-specific prompts. This ensures resilience to article structure variability.
- extract_key_facts ↔ summarize_article_section/for_query: The extracted facts act as a cross-check against the summaries. If control methods extracted do not appear in the control summary, a re-summarization is triggered with a more focused query.

Scenario-based dependencies and decision points:
- Article selection decision: From search_wikipedia outputs, the agent must choose the first title matching inclusion criteria (species name plus invasion/region context). Fallback to the species' main page if no invasion-specific page is found. This selection governs all downstream calls.
- Category coverage decisions: For each of five categories, the presence or absence of matching sections (from get_sections) dictates whether summarize_article_section or summarize_article_for_query is used. This creates five parallel decision paths per species.
- Cross-validation branching: After producing summaries, extract_key_facts (twice per species: impact and control) must be compared to control summaries; if no overlap in methods is detected, the agent must re-run summarize_article_for_query with a refined query (branching loop) and update the control section.
- Link mining integration: get_links provides a large, unstructured list that must be filtered by a specified keyword set. The filtered link titles are used to name concrete management approaches. These results must be reconciled with extract_key_facts and summaries to ensure at least one method is confirmed by both sources.
- Related topics validation: get_related_topics results are used to corroborate vectors and management themes (e.g., presence of "Ballast water" for zebra mussels). If no corroborating related topics are found and earlier steps are weak (e.g., control and introduction both came from fallbacks), the agent must loop back to re-summarize with region-specific queries, introducing an iterative refinement dependency.
- Sparse-page fallback: If get_sections yields zero relevant sections for all categories, the agent must use get_article to access full content and then rely solely on summarize_article_for_query for all categories before proceeding to fact extraction, link mining, and related topics. This is a deep fallback chain.

Parallel vs sequential requirements:
- Per species, the initial discovery chain (search_wikipedia → get_summary → get_sections) is sequential and foundational; downstream category analyses can proceed in parallel once sections are known. However, cross-validation with extract_key_facts and get_related_topics requires all category summaries to be present before checking overlaps and corroboration.
- Across species, the workflow replicates in parallel, but the final cross-species comparison is sequential and depends on all three species' analyses being completed.

Data flow patterns:
- Titles discovered by search_wikipedia determine parameters for all other tools.
- Section titles from get_sections directly parameterize summarize_article_section calls.
- The lack of sections triggers alternate parameterization for summarize_article_for_query (with fixed, provided queries).
- Outputs from extract_key_facts and get_links are combined to assemble management approach lists; get_related_topics is used to validate and optionally trigger re-summarization if corroboration is insufficient.

Cross-server considerations:
- Only the Wikipedia server is available; therefore, all cross-validation occurs within Wikipedia using multiple tools. No external systems are referenced. The logic ensures that if one Wikipedia endpoint yields sparse or non-specific information, another Wikipedia endpoint (e.g., summarize_article_for_query or get_article) is used as a fallback to maintain completeness.

Overall, this design enforces a deep, multi-branch dependency chain with iterative refinement and cross-validation, ensuring the task cannot be completed without understanding the interplay among search, section discovery, targeted summarization, fact extraction, link mining, and related topic validation on Wikipedia.

task_description:
Research objective: Build a validated, comparative, and contradiction-aware brief on the spread pathways, regional distributions, ecological/economic impacts, and control measures of Dreissena polymorpha (zebra mussel) and Dreissena bugensis (quagga mussel), focusing on North America and Europe. Enrich and cross-validate control measures with ballast-water-related topics. Produce a structured JSON synthesis with corroborated items, contradictions, and remaining uncertainties.

Constraints and constants:
- Focal species: ["Zebra mussel", "Quagga mussel"]
- Regions: ["North America", "Europe"]
- Thematic synonyms mapping:
  - Distribution: ["Distribution", "Range", "Geographic distribution", "Geography", "Spread"]
  - Impacts: ["Impact", "Impacts", "Environmental impact", "Effects", "Ecological impact", "Economic impact"]
  - Control: ["Control", "Management", "Prevention", "Mitigation", "Eradication"]
- Related topic relevance keywords: ["invasive", "species", "ballast", "water", "management", "biofouling", "control", "prevention"]
- Section summary max_length: 250
- Query summary max_length: 250
- extract_key_facts counts: primary=7; fallback=10
- Corroboration rule for control measures: include only if present in ≥2 distinct sources among: zebra article, quagga article, ballast-water-related articles set (defined below)
- Minimum corroborated control measures required: 3; if <3, trigger search fallback
- Search fallback queries: ["Zebra mussel control", "Quagga mussel management"] with limit=5
- Contradiction-flagging heuristics for regional distribution/impact: flag if (a) one species article summary/keys mention "widespread" for a region while the other mentions "limited"/"localized" for the same region, or (b) country lists appear inconsistent between species, or (c) impact severity adjectives strongly diverge (e.g., "severe" vs "minor").
- Output must be a single JSON object with the schema described at the end.

Execution plan (mandatory steps and tool sequencing):
1) Identify canonical article titles
   a) Call Wikipedia:search_wikipedia for query="Zebra mussel" with limit=5.
   b) Call Wikipedia:search_wikipedia for query="Quagga mussel" with limit=5.
   c) Selection rule: choose the item with an exact title match if present; else choose the top result for each query. Record chosen titles under articles_processed.source_titles.

2) Inspect structure and locate thematic sections for each chosen article title T in [T_zebra, T_quagga]
   a) Call Wikipedia:get_sections with title=T.
   b) For each theme in [Distribution, Impacts, Control], attempt to match the theme to any section whose title is in the synonyms list for that theme (case-insensitive exact match or section title contains the synonym substring). Record matched section titles; if none matched for a theme, mark theme as "no_section_found" for T.

3) Extract thematic content for each article T and each theme
   a) If a section was found for a theme with matched section title S:
      - Call Wikipedia:summarize_article_section with title=T, section_title=S, max_length=250; store as section_summary.
   b) If no section was found for a theme:
      - Construct thematic queries for summarize_article_for_query:
        • For Distribution: create two queries "Distribution in North America" and "Distribution in Europe"; call Wikipedia:summarize_article_for_query with title=T, query each constructed query, max_length=250; store both.
        • For Impacts: query="Impacts"; call summarize_article_for_query with title=T, query="Impacts", max_length=250.
        • For Control: query="Control and management"; call summarize_article_for_query with title=T, query="Control and management", max_length=250.
   c) For every theme regardless of section presence:
      - Call Wikipedia:extract_key_facts with title=T, topic_within_article set to the theme label ("Distribution", "Impacts", or "Control"), count=7. If fewer than 4 relevant facts can be parsed from the tool output for that theme (you decide relevance by simple keyword presence: for Distribution require words like "range", "present", "introduced", country/region names; for Impacts require words like "impact", "damage", "ecological", "economic"; for Control require words like "control", "manage", "prevent", "eradicate"), then call extract_key_facts again with count=10 and re-evaluate relevance. Retain all relevant facts and note the count.

4) Gather link-based and related-topic enrichments for spread pathways/control context
   a) For each article T in [T_zebra, T_quagga], call Wikipedia:get_links with title=T. From the returned links, collect any titles that string-match (case-insensitive) any of the following substrings: ["ballast", "Ballast water", "International Convention for the Control and Management of Ships' Ballast Water and Sediments", "biofouling", "invasive species"]. Deduplicate across both species. The resulting set is L_candidates.
   b) For each title L in L_candidates:
      - Call Wikipedia:get_summary with title=L.
      - Keep L only if its summary contains at least one keyword from the relevance list ["invasive", "species", "ballast", "water", "management", "biofouling", "control", "prevention"]. The kept set is L_relevant.
   c) For each title L in L_relevant:
      - Call Wikipedia:get_related_topics with title=L, limit=5 to discover additional topics R.
      - For each title R_i in R: call Wikipedia:get_summary with title=R_i and retain R_i only if its summary contains at least one relevance keyword. The union of all retained R_i across L is R_relevant.
   d) The ballast-water-related articles set for corroboration is B = L_relevant ∪ R_relevant (deduplicated). Record all items in B under related_topics and store their brief summaries.

5) Corroborate control measures across sources
   a) From step 3 for both species, collect control-related facts and section/query summaries. Normalize control mentions by lowercasing and trimming; treat near-duplicates with minor wording differences as the same measure if they share a core phrase (e.g., "ballast water treatment" matches "treatment of ballast water").
   b) From set B (step 4d), scan summaries for explicit control/prevention measures (e.g., "ballast water exchange", "filtration", "UV treatment", "chlorination", "dry docking", "public education", "decontamination protocols").
   c) Include a control measure in the final corroborated list only if it appears in ≥2 sources among {zebra article, quagga article, any item in B}. If fewer than 3 measures satisfy this, perform the search fallback:
      - Call Wikipedia:search_wikipedia for each query in ["Zebra mussel control", "Quagga mussel management"] with limit=5. For any returned title not already in {T_zebra, T_quagga} ∪ B, call Wikipedia:get_summary and scan for measures; add any measure found to the source pool; recompute corroboration.

6) Build region-specific distribution and impact synopses and flag contradictions
   a) For each region in ["North America", "Europe"], synthesize a region summary by combining distribution-related section/query summaries and relevant key facts from both species. Include specific countries or water systems if mentioned.
   b) For impacts, synthesize per-region impacts by combining impacts-related summaries and facts from both species.
   c) Apply contradiction-flagging heuristics: if language between species for the same region diverges (e.g., "widespread" vs "limited"), or country lists do not overlap as expected, or severity adjectives diverge markedly, add an entry under contradictions with fields: {region, theme (Distribution/Impacts), species_pair, evidence_snippets, reason}.

7) Final output format (must be a single JSON object with these keys):
- articles_processed: {
    zebra: { title, sections: [ ...section titles... ] },
    quagga: { title, sections: [ ...section titles... ] }
  }
- themes: {
    Distribution: {
      zebra: { section_summary_or_queries: { section_title or queries: [...], text: "..." }, key_facts: [ ... ] },
      quagga: { ... }
    },
    Impacts: { zebra: { ... }, quagga: { ... } },
    Control: { zebra: { ... }, quagga: { ... } }
  }
- related_topics: {
    from_links_relevant: [ { title, summary }... ],
    related_expanded: [ { title, summary, parent: <from which L> }... ]
  }
- control_measures_corroborated: [ { measure, sources: [titles], corroboration_count }... ]
- regional_summaries: {
    "North America": { distribution: "...", impacts: "..." },
    "Europe": { distribution: "...", impacts: "..." }
  }
- contradictions: [ { region, theme, species_pair: ["zebra", "quagga"], evidence_snippets: ["...", "..."], reason }... ]
- uncertainties: [ three concise bullets capturing ambiguities or gaps detected during extraction and cross-validation ]

Notes:
- Use every specified tool where indicated. Follow all decision rules and fallbacks. Do not fetch any external resources beyond the provided tools. Ensure deduplication of titles in related topics. Ensure all thresholds and counts above are enforced.
dependency_analysis:
Inherent dependencies and tool chains:
- Wikipedia:search_wikipedia → title selection → downstream tools require the chosen titles (Wikipedia:get_sections, Wikipedia:summarize_article_section, Wikipedia:extract_key_facts, Wikipedia:get_links, Wikipedia:get_related_topics, Wikipedia:get_summary). This establishes the canonical entry points for both species.
- Wikipedia:get_sections informs whether to use Wikipedia:summarize_article_section (if a matching section exists) or fall back to Wikipedia:summarize_article_for_query (if not). This creates a conditional dependency where the presence/absence of sections gates which summarization tool is appropriate.
- Wikipedia:get_links outputs article titles that become inputs to Wikipedia:get_summary (for filtering relevance via keyword criteria) and then to Wikipedia:get_related_topics (to expand the topic graph). The related topics (and their summaries) feed back into the control-measure corroboration step, creating a multi-hop dependency chain: base article → links → summaries (filter) → related topics → summaries (filter) → inclusion in the corroboration source set.
- Wikipedia:extract_key_facts depends on the same base article titles, with topic_within_article steering extraction towards Distribution/Impacts/Control. If the number of relevant facts is insufficient (<4), an iterative dependency triggers a second call to the same tool with a higher count (10), and, if necessary, reliance on summarize_article_for_query text to supplement understanding.

Scenario-based dependencies and decision points:
- Title selection decision: The output of Wikipedia:search_wikipedia determines the exact canonical article title. If an exact match is absent, the top result is used—this affects all subsequent calls.
- Section presence decision: The output of Wikipedia:get_sections (section titles) determines whether to use Wikipedia:summarize_article_section (preferred, if section exists) or Wikipedia:summarize_article_for_query (fallback), injecting a branching path per theme (Distribution/Impacts/Control) per article.
- Relevance filter decision: The output of Wikipedia:get_links seeds candidate titles that are filtered using Wikipedia:get_summary via keyword rules. Only titles whose summaries contain relevant keywords are kept, gating the call to Wikipedia:get_related_topics. Then, related topics are again filtered using Wikipedia:get_summary. Thus, summaries act as validation checkpoints for inclusion in the corroboration pool.
- Iterative refinement decision: The count of relevant key facts from Wikipedia:extract_key_facts determines whether a second, higher-count extraction is needed. If still insufficient, summarize_article_for_query outputs are used to supplement thematic content.
- Corroboration fallback decision: If fewer than 3 control measures meet the ≥2-source corroboration rule (validated across zebra, quagga, and ballast-water-related sets), the pipeline triggers a search fallback (Wikipedia:search_wikipedia on two specified queries) and subsequent Wikipedia:get_summary calls on new titles to augment the control-source pool.
- Contradiction detection: The synthesized distributions and impacts (from section summaries, query summaries, and key facts) are compared across species within each region. Divergent descriptors or inconsistent country lists lead to contradictions being recorded. This step relies on earlier tool outputs and text processing, and its outcome affects the contradictions section in the final report.

Parallel vs sequential execution:
- Parallelizable components: After canonical titles are chosen, per-article workflows (sections, summaries, key facts, links) can run in parallel for zebra and quagga. Within each article, the three themes (Distribution, Impacts, Control) can be processed in parallel because they are independent branches using the same inputs (title, sections). Link-based enrichment for both articles can also proceed in parallel and then be merged.
- Sequential dependencies: Title selection must precede all per-article operations. Section detection must precede the choice between summarize_article_section and summarize_article_for_query. Link extraction must precede related-topic expansion. The corroboration step requires that species thematic extractions and ballast-water-related expansions are complete. Contradiction analysis requires that regional synopses are synthesized.

Cross-server dependencies:
- Only a single server (Wikipedia) is provided in this task. Therefore, cross-server dependencies are not applicable. Instead, cross-article dependencies within the Wikipedia server are leveraged: base species articles inform link discovery which informs related-topic expansion, and these feed back into corroboration for control measures.

Data flow summary:
- search_wikipedia (zebra, quagga) → canonical titles → get_sections (per title) → decision: summarize_article_section vs summarize_article_for_query (per theme) → extract_key_facts (iterative counts) → get_links (per title) → get_summary (filter L_candidates) → get_related_topics (per relevant L) → get_summary (filter related) → assemble B (ballast-water-related set) → corroborate control measures (≥2 sources) with fallback search_wikipedia + get_summary if needed → synthesize regional summaries (North America, Europe) using thematic results → detect contradictions using heuristic rules → produce final structured JSON.

All tools from the available server are incorporated with explicit dependencies, branching logic, iterative refinement, and validation gates to ensure the task cannot be completed correctly without understanding and executing the specified tool chains.

task_description:
Goal: Produce an executive brief (max 600 words) for the upcoming week that explains the El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO) mechanism, the principal indices used to monitor it (ONI and SOI) with validated definitions, key related/teleconnected phenomena, and region-specific impacts (Australia, Peru, Southern United States). The brief must be constructed solely from Wikipedia using the provided tools, follow the dependency logic below, and include explicit source mapping (titles and sections used). Deliverable structure: 1) Executive summary (<=120 words), 2) Mechanism (<=150 words), 3) Monitoring indices (bullets, each tagged [validated by multiple pages], [partial], or [conflict]), 4) Related phenomena (3 items, 1–2 sentences each), 5) Regional impacts (Australia, Peru, Southern United States; 3 bullets each), 6) Sources (list page titles used and the exact sections summarized).

Strict workflow and decision logic (use exact queries and thresholds as specified):

Step 1 — Identify core ENSO page (sequential):
- Use Wikipedia:search_wikipedia with query "El Niño–Southern Oscillation" and limit 5.
- If the exact title isn’t returned, search again with query "ENSO" (limit 5) and select the page whose summary mentions this is a climate pattern involving El Niño and La Niña.
- Record the selected title as CORE_TITLE.

Step 2 — Locate mechanism section (dependent on Step 1):
- Use Wikipedia:get_sections on CORE_TITLE.
- From the returned sections, select the first section whose title string contains any of the case-insensitive keywords: ["Mechanism", "Dynamics", "Physical mechanism"]. Store as MECH_SECTION.
- If no match, set MECH_SECTION to null and proceed with fallback in Step 3.

Step 3 — Summarize mechanism (dependent on Step 2):
- If MECH_SECTION is not null, call Wikipedia:summarize_article_section on CORE_TITLE with section_title=MECH_SECTION and max_length=260 to produce the mechanism summary.
- Else, call Wikipedia:summarize_article_for_query on CORE_TITLE with query="mechanism and dynamics of ENSO (Bjerknes feedback, Kelvin and Rossby waves, Walker circulation)" and max_length=260.

Step 4 — Confirm Bjerknes feedback mention (validation branch):
- Use Wikipedia:get_article on CORE_TITLE and search the returned content text for the phrase "Bjerknes feedback" (case-insensitive).
- If found, mark Bjerknes feedback as referenced in the core article.
- If not found, use Wikipedia:search_wikipedia with query "Bjerknes feedback" (limit 5), pick the best-matching title, and call Wikipedia:get_summary on that title; include it later under Related phenomena even if not present in CORE_TITLE, tagging it as "not explicitly referenced in core article".

Step 5 — Extract core indices mentions from CORE_TITLE (feeds Step 6):
- Use Wikipedia:summarize_article_for_query on CORE_TITLE with query="indices used to monitor ENSO (ONI, SOI) and thresholds" and max_length=200. Store as CORE_INDICES_SUMMARY.

Step 6 — Index definitions and cross-validation (multi-article, sequential + validation):
- For Southern Oscillation Index (SOI):
  - Use Wikipedia:search_wikipedia with query "Southern Oscillation Index" (limit 5). Select the best-matching title as SOI_TITLE.
  - Call Wikipedia:get_summary on SOI_TITLE.
  - Call Wikipedia:extract_key_facts on SOI_TITLE with topic_within_article="definition and threshold" and count=5.
  - Validation rule for SOI: Mark as [validated by multiple pages] only if both the SOI page (summary or key facts) and CORE_INDICES_SUMMARY mention the pressure difference between Tahiti and Darwin. If mentioned in only one source, tag [partial]. If contradictions arise (e.g., a different station pair), tag [conflict].
- For Oceanic Niño Index (ONI):
  - Use Wikipedia:search_wikipedia with query "Oceanic Niño Index" (limit 5). Select the best-matching title as ONI_TITLE.
  - Call Wikipedia:get_summary on ONI_TITLE.
  - Call Wikipedia:extract_key_facts on ONI_TITLE with topic_within_article="Niño 3.4, 3-month running mean, ±0.5°C thresholds" and count=5.
  - Validation rule for ONI: Mark as [validated by multiple pages] only if both the ONI page (summary or key facts) and CORE_INDICES_SUMMARY confirm that ONI is based on the 3-month running mean of SST anomalies in the Niño 3.4 region and that ±0.5°C thresholds define El Niño/La Niña events. If only one source confirms thresholds, tag [partial]. If discrepancies on thresholds or region arise, tag [conflict].

Step 7 — Discover related/teleconnected phenomena (links-driven with fallback; parallelizable per item):
- Use Wikipedia:get_links on CORE_TITLE.
- From the returned link titles, select up to three items by this priority order: ["Teleconnection (climate)", "Walker circulation", "Madden–Julian oscillation", "Pacific Decadal Oscillation", "Kelvin wave", "Rossby wave", "Bjerknes feedback"]. Preserve order.
- For each selected title, call Wikipedia:get_summary to obtain a concise definition.
- If "Teleconnection (climate)" is not present in the get_links result:
  - Use Wikipedia:get_related_topics on CORE_TITLE (limit 10) to find a teleconnection-related topic. If found, summarize it with Wikipedia:get_summary.
  - If still not found, use Wikipedia:search_wikipedia with query "Teleconnection" (limit 5), pick the climate-related title, and summarize it.

Step 8 — Regional impacts (two-page triangulation; dependent on searches):
- Identify the El Niño page:
  - Use Wikipedia:search_wikipedia with query "El Niño" (limit 5); select the canonical El Niño article as ELNINO_TITLE.
- Identify the La Niña page:
  - Use Wikipedia:search_wikipedia with query "La Niña" (limit 5); select the canonical La Niña article as LANINA_TITLE.
- For each of ELNINO_TITLE and LANINA_TITLE, call Wikipedia:get_sections.
  - Try to locate a section with any of these case-insensitive keywords: ["Impacts", "Effects", "Regional impacts"]. If found, call Wikipedia:summarize_article_section with max_length=180 (once per title).
  - If none are found for a title, call Wikipedia:summarize_article_for_query on that title with query="impacts on Australia, Peru, and Southern United States" and max_length=180.
- From these summaries, extract concise, evidence-based bullets for each region:
  - Australia: typical rainfall and drought/flood tendency under El Niño and under La Niña.
  - Peru: typical rainfall anomalies and fisheries impacts (El Niño focus; note La Niña if present).
  - Southern United States: typical winter precipitation and temperature anomalies under El Niño vs La Niña.
- If El Niño and La Niña sources disagree on the sign or prevalence of an impact for a given region, present both and tag the item [conflict], citing which page provided which claim (by title only).

Step 9 — Assemble the final brief (format requirement):
- Section 1: Executive summary (<=120 words) — synthesize mechanism, monitoring approach (ONI, SOI), and high-level teleconnections and regional risk pointers for the upcoming week.
- Section 2: ENSO mechanism (<=150 words) — use output from Step 3 and note whether Bjerknes feedback was explicitly mentioned in CORE_TITLE (from Step 4).
- Section 3: Monitoring indices — two bullets for ONI and SOI. For each, include a one-sentence definition plus thresholds (if available), and the tag [validated by multiple pages], [partial], or [conflict] according to Step 6.
- Section 4: Related phenomena — three items from Step 7; each 1–2 sentences with a clear relevance note to ENSO.
- Section 5: Regional impacts — three sublists (Australia, Peru, Southern United States) with three bullets each reflecting El Niño vs La Niña differences. Include [conflict] tags where applicable per Step 8.
- Section 6: Sources — list all Wikipedia titles used and, where applicable, the exact section titles summarized (from Steps 3 and 8). Do not include URLs.

Constraints and notes:
- Use only the specified tools. No external data sources or URLs.
- Do not invent content. If a required detail is missing, mark it as [partial] and proceed.
- Maintain the specified word and bullet limits.
- All searches must use exactly the queries given above with the stated limits.
- The brief is intended for the upcoming week (relative time marker); do not include time-specific forecasts, only canonical mechanisms and impacts inferred from Wikipedia.
dependency_analysis:
Inherent dependencies and tool chains:
- Standard discovery pipeline: Wikipedia:search_wikipedia → Wikipedia:get_sections → Wikipedia:summarize_article_section. The search identifies the canonical article title(s); the section list is then used to choose specific section titles, which are required parameters for summarize_article_section.
- Article-level summary and query-tuned summarization: Wikipedia:get_summary provides quick definitions for related topics, while Wikipedia:summarize_article_for_query targets specific subtopics when sections are missing or ambiguous.

task_description:
Conduct a comparative operational analysis of six major public bicycle-sharing systems using Wikipedia tools only, to derive best-practice recommendations for a hypothetical city planning to launch or upgrade a bike-share program. The systems to analyze are: Vélib' (Paris), Citi Bike (New York City), Hangzhou Public Bicycle (Hangzhou), Santander Cycles (London), Bicing (Barcelona), and Capital Bikeshare (Washington, D.C.). The task must use all available Wikipedia tools in a multi-step, decision-driven workflow with fallbacks and iterative refinement. Follow these concrete steps and parameters:

1) Title disambiguation via search: For each of the six systems, call Wikipedia:search_wikipedia with query set exactly to the system name and limit=5. System names to search: "Vélib'", "Citi Bike", "Hangzhou Public Bicycle", "Santander Cycles", "Bicing", "Capital Bikeshare". Decision rule: select the first result whose title contains the full system name or a clear variant (e.g., "Vélib' Métropole" qualifies for Vélib'). If no clear match appears in the top 5, re-run search_wikipedia with the query "[System Name] bike share" and limit=10, then select the best matching title.

2) Core article retrieval and section mapping: For each selected title, call Wikipedia:get_article to fetch full content, and Wikipedia:get_sections to list sections. Decision rules and fallbacks:
- History section: If a section titled any of {"History", "Background", "Origins"} exists, call Wikipedia:summarize_article_section with max_length=200 on that section. Else call Wikipedia:summarize_article_for_query with query="history and launch timeline" and max_length=250.
- Operations section: If any of {"Operations", "System", "Technology", "Infrastructure"} exists, call Wikipedia:summarize_article_section with max_length=200. Else call Wikipedia:summarize_article_for_query with query="operations and logistics including docks, bikes, rebalancing" and max_length=250.
- Criticism/Issues: If any of {"Criticism", "Controversies", "Issues", "Challenges"} exists, call Wikipedia:summarize_article_section with max_length=200. Else call Wikipedia:summarize_article_for_query with query="controversies, vandalism, theft, safety incidents" and max_length=250.

3) Key facts extraction and numeric metric recovery: For each article, call Wikipedia:extract_key_facts with count=7 and topic_within_article="ridership, fleet size, station count, pricing model, operator". If fewer than 5 distinct facts are returned OR if the returned facts do not include numbers for any of these target metrics, run up to five targeted calls to Wikipedia:summarize_article_for_query (max_length=120 each) with the following queries: "annual ridership numbers", "number of bicycles (fleet size)", "number of stations", "pricing model (subscription/pay-as-you-go)", "operator (ownership/management)". If still missing numeric values after these queries, run Wikipedia:get_summary for the article and parse for any numbers; if none, note the metric as "not available via article text".

4) Links and related topics cross-validation: For each article, call Wikipedia:get_links and Wikipedia:get_related_topics (limit=10). From the union of links and related topics, select up to 3 items relevant to operational or policy context from this target set and synonyms: {"Bicycle-sharing system", "Dockless bicycle sharing", "Micromobility", "Vandalism", "Bicycle theft", "Smart bike", "Bike rental", "Electric bicycle", "Pedelec", "Redistribution"}. Selection decision: choose the first three that appear in either list and are closest to the system’s issues seen in Step 2 (e.g., if controversies mention vandalism, prioritize "Vandalism" or "Bicycle theft"). For each selected topic:
- Call Wikipedia:get_summary for context.
- Call Wikipedia:summarize_article_for_query with query="relevance to [System Name]" and max_length=150 to connect the topic to the specific system’s operational challenges or features.
If Wikipedia:get_related_topics returns fewer than 5 items, re-call it with limit=15 and re-apply selection.

5) General domain context: Call Wikipedia:get_summary for the title "Bicycle-sharing system" to establish global context and key concepts. Also call Wikipedia:summarize_article_for_query on that article with query="operational models (docked vs dockless) and rebalancing strategies" and max_length=250.

6) Synthesis and output requirements: Compile findings into a structured report with the following sections:
- Overview: 5-7 bullet points summarizing the global context from "Bicycle-sharing system" and cross-topic insights.
- Per-system profiles (six subsections): For each system, include bullet points for launch/overview, operations, controversies/issues, and 5 target metrics: launch year (if available), fleet size, station count, annual ridership, pricing model, operator. Include any notable technology (e.g., smart locks, RFID) and whether the system is docked, dockless, or hybrid. If any metric is unavailable after Step 3, mark it explicitly as "not available via article text".
- Cross-cutting issues: 8-10 bullet points identifying common pitfalls and successful strategies across systems (e.g., vandalism mitigation, redistribution logistics, pricing elasticity, technology reliability, integration with public transit). Where relevant, cite which related topic summaries informed these points (by article title).
- Recommendations: Provide 5 concrete, actionable best practices for a new or upgrading city system, grounded in evidence from the above analyses.
- Audit trail: Provide a chronological list of every tool call performed, including the exact parameters (query/title/limits/max_length/count) and a one-line note of the decision criterion that triggered each call or fallback.

Constraints and execution notes:
- Use only the specified Wikipedia tools. Do not reference or call any external APIs, files, databases, or non-Wikipedia servers.
- All queries, titles, limits, counts, and max_length values are provided above; do not ask for additional inputs.
- Execute the workflow even if some articles lack certain sections; rely on the defined fallbacks. Ensure all nine tools are used at least once across the complete task.
- Parallelization is allowed for per-system processing, but synthesis must consolidate across all systems.
- The output must be plain text with bullet lists; avoid heavy formatting.
dependency_analysis:
Inherent tool dependencies and workflow patterns:
- Wikipedia:search_wikipedia → Wikipedia:get_article → Wikipedia:get_sections form the foundational discovery-to-structure chain: search provides candidate titles; get_article is necessary for content; get_sections reveals article organization and determines whether section-targeted summaries are possible.
- Wikipedia:get_sections → Wikipedia:summarize_article_section: section enumeration drives targeted summarization; if the desired sections exist, section summarization is preferred for precision.
- Wikipedia:get_article and get_summary provide raw and concise content; when sections are missing, Wikipedia:summarize_article_for_query tailors extraction to specific operational questions.
- Wikipedia:extract_key_facts consumes the article title and optionally topic focus to produce concise metrics; its outputs (or lack thereof) trigger further tailored summarization calls.
- Wikipedia:get_links and Wikipedia:get_related_topics operate in parallel to surface contextual articles; their outputs determine which additional summaries to fetch for cross-validation.

Scenario-based dependencies and decision logic:
- Title selection dependency: The choice of the correct article title for each system depends on search results. If the first search does not yield an exact/clear variant, a second search with broadened query and higher limit occurs; the selected title feeds all subsequent tools for that system.
- Section-driven branching: Presence or absence of specific sections (History, Operations, Criticism/Issues) determines whether summarize_article_section is used or whether the agent must fall back to summarize_article_for_query with predefined queries.
- Metric completeness gating: The results of extract_key_facts are inspected for count and numeric detail. If insufficient, a sequence of summarize_article_for_query calls targets each missing metric. If still lacking, get_summary is used as a final fallback to attempt to recover numbers; failing that, metrics are marked unavailable.
- Contextual topic selection: get_links and get_related_topics run in parallel; their union is filtered against a predefined relevance set and the specific issues discovered in Step 2. Selected topics then drive additional get_summary and summarize_article_for_query calls to build cross-cutting insights.
- Domain baseline: A separate get_summary and summarize_article_for_query call on "Bicycle-sharing system" anchors the analysis with general operational models and rebalancing strategies.

Parallel vs. sequential requirements:
- Parallel: The per-system pipelines (Steps 1–4) can run concurrently, each following search → fetch → section analysis → facts extraction → contextual expansion.
- Sequential: Within each system pipeline, calls are ordered: search precedes get_article; get_sections precedes section summarization; extract_key_facts precedes targeted metric queries; contextual topic selection precedes topic summarization. The synthesis (Step 6) occurs after all system pipelines and domain context are complete.

Critical decision points:
- Choosing correct article titles based on search results.
- Deciding section-based summarization vs. query-based summarization depending on section presence.
- Determining metric completeness and invoking fallbacks.
- Selecting the most relevant related/link topics tied to discovered issues per system.
- Merging per-system and cross-topic findings into coherent, evidence-backed recommendations.

Cross-server dependencies:
- Not applicable; only the Wikipedia server is available. All cross-validation and contextualization are performed within the Wikipedia tools ecosystem by combining outputs from search, article content, sections, summaries, links, and related topics.

Data flow summary:
- Inputs: fixed system names and predefined queries/parameters.
- Flow: search_wikipedia (titles) → get_article (content) → get_sections (structure) → summarize_article_section or summarize_article_for_query (targeted extraction) → extract_key_facts (metrics) → conditional summarize_article_for_query/get_summary (metric recovery) → get_links/get_related_topics (context expansion) → get_summary/summarize_article_for_query for selected topics (contextual insights) → synthesis (report and audit trail).
