task_description:
Objective: Produce a source-backed research brief for a museum planning team on Traditional Polynesian navigation techniques, key figures and vessels, and the modern revival, using only the provided Wikipedia tools. The brief must include technique summaries, notable people/vessels, subtopic deep-dives, cross-validated claims, and a related-topic map. All steps, decisions, and tool call counts must be documented. Final deliverable format is a single JSON object as specified below.

Core topic and scope: Traditional Polynesian navigation (wayfinding without instruments), including core methods (stars, swells, birds, clouds, currents), exemplars (e.g., Hōkūleʻa), and figures (e.g., Mau Piailug, Nainoa Thompson). No external sources permitted.

Required search queries (use exactly as strings):
- "Polynesian navigation"
- "Traditional Polynesian navigation"
- "Wayfinding (navigation)"
- "Micronesian navigation"
- "Hōkūleʻa"
- "Mau Piailug"
- "Polynesian Voyaging Society"

Tool workflow and constraints:
1) Primary article selection (sequential):
   a) Use Wikipedia:search_wikipedia with query="Polynesian navigation" and limit=5. Capture all returned titles.
   b) If no exact title match for "Polynesian navigation" is found, also run Wikipedia:search_wikipedia with query="Traditional Polynesian navigation" and limit=5, then with query="Wayfinding (navigation)" and limit=5.
   c) Determine a primary article title by this priority order:
      - P1: Exact title "Polynesian navigation" (preferred)
      - P2: Any title containing the phrase "Polynesian navigation"
      - P3: Title "Wayfinding (navigation)" if its summary mentions Polynesia or Pacific traditional wayfinding
      - P4: Title "Micronesian navigation" if neither P1–P3 is viable
   d) For P3/P4 decisions, fetch candidate summaries via Wikipedia:get_summary to check mention criteria. Record which branch triggered and why.

2) Primary article deep read and techniques extraction (sequential with fallback):
   a) Call Wikipedia:get_article on the chosen primary title.
   b) Call Wikipedia:get_sections on that title to enumerate section titles.
   c) If any section title contains any of these keywords (case-insensitive): ["Techniques", "Methods", "Principles"], pick the most specific one (longest title string) and call Wikipedia:summarize_article_section with max_length=200.
   d) Else call Wikipedia:summarize_article_for_query with query="Core techniques of traditional Polynesian navigation: stars, swells, birds, clouds, currents, star compass; how navigators infer direction and position" and max_length=250.
   e) Store this as techniques_summary.

3) Notable people and vessels (sequential with conditional fallback using links):
   a) Run Wikipedia:extract_key_facts on the primary article with topic_within_article="Notable navigators and vessels" and count=7.
   b) Evaluate if at least 3 distinct proper names appear among the facts. Proper name heuristic: contains at least one space and initial uppercase on both words (e.g., "Mau Piailug", "Nainoa Thompson"), or is a capitalized vessel or organization name from this allowlist: ["Hōkūleʻa", "Polynesian Voyaging Society"].
   c) If fewer than 3 proper names found, run Wikipedia:get_links on the primary title. From the returned link titles, select up to 5 that contain any of these tokens (case-insensitive): ["Hōkūle", "Piailug", "Thompson", "Voyaging Society", "Micronesian"]. For each selected link title, call Wikipedia:get_summary and extract 1–2 identifying facts focused on role/contribution to Polynesian navigation. Combine with any facts from step 3a to produce a list of 4–7 entries. Each entry must have fields: name, one_sentence_summary, source_title.

4) Related topics and subtopic deep-dives (sequential then parallelizable per subtopic):
   a) Call Wikipedia:get_related_topics on the primary title with limit=15. Record the list.
   b) Select up to 3 subtopics by this priority order: titles containing (in order) "Hōkūle", "Mau Piailug", "Micronesian navigation", "Polynesian Voyaging Society"; if fewer than 3 found, fill remaining slots with titles that contain either "navigation" or "canoe" (case-insensitive) from the related topics list.
   c) For each selected subtopic title:
      - Call Wikipedia:get_article and Wikipedia:get_sections on it.
      - If it has any of these sections: ["Voyages", "History", "Techniques"], for each present section call Wikipedia:summarize_article_section with max_length=150 and store as section_summaries (array of {section_title, summary}).
      - Else call Wikipedia:summarize_article_for_query with query="Key contributions of this topic to Polynesian wayfinding and the modern revival (notable voyages, training, techniques)" and max_length=200 and store as a single item in section_summaries with section_title="Query-focused summary".
      - Additionally, call Wikipedia:extract_key_facts with count=3 on each subtopic and store as key_facts.

5) Cross-validation of critical claims (sequential with branching):
   a) Evaluate the presence of the following candidate claims by checking at least two distinct article titles among: the primary and the chosen subtopics. For each claim, use Wikipedia:summarize_article_for_query with max_length=120 on each relevant article to detect mention evidence:
      - C1: "Use of a star compass as a core method"
      - C2: "Reading ocean swells/wave patterns to infer direction"
      - C3: "Hōkūleʻa completed a worldwide voyage"
      - C4: "Mau Piailug mentored Nainoa Thompson"
   b) For each claim, if two or more distinct article summaries explicitly or implicitly support the claim, mark it corroborated=true and list the supporting titles. If fewer than two, mark corroborated=false and list any partial evidence.
   c) If C3 is not corroborated, attempt to replace it by validating instead: C5: "Modern revival of Polynesian navigation led by the Polynesian Voyaging Society" using the same method.

6) Related topic overview (sequential):
   a) From step 4a results, select exactly 5 related topics (prioritize diversity: aim to include at least one person, one vessel, one organization, and one technique if possible based on titles). Provide titles only.

7) Documentation and reproducibility (sequential):
   a) Record a decision_log explaining: primary selection branch; whether a techniques section existed; whether fallback in step 3 was needed; which subtopics were chosen and why; which claims were corroborated and why/not.
   b) Count and report tool_calls by tool name.
   c) Provide search_queries_used as the exact list of strings executed.

Expected final output JSON (single object) must include exactly these top-level fields:
- primary_article_title: string
- techniques_summary: string
- notable_people_and_vessels: array of 4–7 objects with fields {name, one_sentence_summary, source_title}
- subtopic_summaries: array of 2–3 objects with fields {title, section_summaries: array of {section_title, summary}, key_facts: array of strings}
- cross_validated_claims: array of 3–4 objects with fields {claim, corroborated: boolean, sources: array of titles}
- related_topics_overview: array of exactly 5 strings (titles)
- decision_log: string (concise narrative of branches and reasons)
- tool_calls: object where keys are tool names and values are integers
- search_queries_used: array of strings

Notes:
- All steps must be executed using only the provided Wikipedia tools.
- Selection thresholds and token checks are specified above and must be followed exactly.
- If any tool call fails for a particular title, skip that title and note the skip in decision_log.
- No external URLs, files, dates, or systems are allowed.
dependency_analysis:
Inherent tool dependencies and standard flows:
- Search → Fetch → Analyze: search_wikipedia identifies candidate titles; get_article/get_summary then provide source content; get_sections/guided summaries/extract_key_facts analyze content. This core chain underpins most steps.
- Article structure introspection: get_sections informs whether summarize_article_section or summarize_article_for_query should be used for the techniques content (section-aware vs query-focused summarization).
- Relationship mapping: get_related_topics and get_links mine the article graph to select subtopics and, if needed, to rescue missing notable entities.

Scenario-based dependencies and decision points:
- Primary article selection (Step 1) is a multi-branch decision: search_wikipedia outputs determine whether we can pick an exact match (P1/P2). If not, get_summary outputs for candidates control the choice between P3 (Wayfinding) and P4 (Micronesian navigation). Thus, tool B (get_summary) depends on tool A (search_wikipedia) and controls the subsequent path.
- Techniques extraction (Step 2) is conditioned on get_sections output: presence of a "Techniques/Methods/Principles" section triggers summarize_article_section; absence triggers summarize_article_for_query. Here, tool choice and parameters are driven by structural data from another tool.
- Notables extraction (Step 3) uses extract_key_facts first; if insufficient proper names are detected, a fallback branch uses get_links → filtering on title tokens → get_summary to synthesize notables. Thus, get_links outputs determine both which titles to fetch and the parameterization of subsequent get_summary calls.
- Subtopic deep-dives (Step 4) are seeded by get_related_topics from the primary article; the selection logic prefers certain titles, else falls back to keyword-based matches. For each selected subtopic, we again use get_sections to conditionally choose summarize_article_section (for targeted sections) or summarize_article_for_query (as a catch-all), then extract_key_facts to collect concise data. This creates a repeated dependency chain with conditional branches per subtopic, enabling parallel execution across subtopics while preserving a shared selection logic.
- Cross-validation (Step 5) explicitly reuses summarize_article_for_query across at least two distinct article contexts (primary + subtopics) to assess specific claims. The corroboration decision (boolean) depends on whether multiple query-focused summaries signal consistent evidence. If claim C3 fails corroboration, a conditional replacement (C5) is attempted, creating a recovery branch.
- Related topics overview (Step 6) depends again on get_related_topics outcomes; the selection requires diversity based on title cues (person/vessel/organization/technique), forcing the agent to interpret title semantics.
- Documentation (Step 7) aggregates decisions and counts across all prior steps, ensuring the agent tracked which branch each dependency chain followed and how many tool invocations occurred per tool.

Parallel vs sequential:
- Sequential phases: primary selection, primary article analysis, and the initial notables and related topics discovery must occur in order, because each phase’s input (title choices, section presence, links) depends on the previous outputs.
- Parallelizable phase: after selecting subtopics (Step 4), each subtopic’s fetch/section/summarize/facts pipeline can be executed independently, then combined.

Data flow highlights:
- Titles flow from search_wikipedia → get_summary/get_article/get_sections; section names flow into summarize_article_section; related topics and links yield new titles consumed by get_article/get_summary; extract_key_facts produces candidate notables and fact lists used directly in the deliverable or as evidence in cross-validation.

Cross-server considerations:
- Only a single server (Wikipedia) is available; therefore, no cross-server dependencies are applicable. All cross-validation and fallback logic occur within the Wikipedia server using multiple complementary tools.

Critical decision thresholds and parameters:
- Primary selection thresholds: priority P1→P4 with summary-based content check for P3/P4.
- Techniques section detection: keyword match ["Techniques", "Methods", "Principles"].
- Notables sufficiency: at least 3 proper names by heuristic; else fallback via get_links + token filter ["Hōkūle", "Piailug", "Thompson", "Voyaging Society", "Micronesian"].
- Subtopic count: up to 3, priority list rules, then keyword fallback.
- Cross-validation: corroboration requires evidence across ≥2 distinct article titles via query-focused summaries.

This task enforces deep understanding of tool dependencies by requiring dynamic selection of tools based on previous outputs, iterative refinement through fallbacks, and multi-article cross-validation using query-tailored summaries. It also mandates the use of every provided Wikipedia tool in a meaningful, interdependent manner.

task_description:
Objective: Build a structured, cross-validated research brief on the rise and global diffusion of containerization in maritime logistics, emphasizing standardization and its economic impact. The brief must be created solely using the provided Wikipedia tools and must include selection logic, fallbacks, and cross-link verification. Use all listed Wikipedia tools at least once in a meaningful dependency chain.

Scope and constraints:
- Topic: Containerization in global shipping logistics (standardized intermodal containers), including standards and diffusion via major ports. Do not include coverage of specific canals.
- All data must originate from Wikipedia tools in this task. Do not use any external sources.
- Use only the following concrete search queries and titles specified below. Do not add new topics beyond those discovered via the specified tool-driven process.
- Follow the decision rules, fallbacks, and cross-validation steps exactly as specified.

Expected final output format (JSON):
{
  "base_article": {
    "title": "...",
    "selected_from_query": "...",
    "matched_sections": ["..."],
    "history_summary": "...",
    "economics_and_standardization_summary": "...",
    "key_facts_standardization": ["...", "...", "...", "...", "..."],
    "key_facts_economics": ["...", "...", "...", "...", "..."]
  },
  "standards": [
    {
      "title": "...",
      "summary": "...",
      "key_facts": ["...", "...", "..."],
      "cross_validated_with_base": true,
      "cross_validation_evidence": {
        "appears_in_related_topics_of_standard": true/false,
        "appears_in_links_of_base": true/false
      }
    }
  ],
  "ports": [
    {
      "title": "...",
      "history_section_summary": "...",
      "role_in_containerization_summary": "..."
    }
  ],
  "person": {
    "title": "Malcom McLean",
    "summary": "...",
    "key_facts": ["...", "...", "...", "...", "..."]
  },
  "relationship_map": {
    "nodes": ["<base>", "<standard_1>", "<standard_2>", "<standard_3>", "<port_1>", "<port_2>", "<port_3>", "<port_4>", "<port_5>", "Malcom McLean"],
    "adjacency": {
      "<node_title>": ["<linked_node_title>", "..."]
    },
    "method": "Edges exist if a node’s get_links includes another node’s exact title."
  },
  "sources": ["<list all article titles queried or fetched>"]
}

Required workflow and tool usage (strictly follow sequencing, dependencies, and decision points):
1) Initial discovery (sequential search):
   - Call Wikipedia:search_wikipedia with each of the following queries (limit = 5):
     a) "Containerization"
     b) "Intermodal container"
     c) "Malcom McLean"
     d) "Twenty-foot equivalent unit"
     e) "Container port"
   - Record the top 5 titles for (a) and (b). You will use (c) later for the person profile. (d) and (e) are used for link/related topic harvesting only.

2) Base-article candidate selection (decision point; dependency on Step 1):
   - For the top 3 titles returned by query (a) "Containerization": call Wikipedia:get_sections on each title.
   - For each candidate, check if its sections contain at least two of the following target section titles (case-insensitive substring match): "History", "Economics", "Impact", "Standards", "Standardization", "Effects".
   - If at least one candidate from (a) matches, select the candidate with the highest count of matching target sections as the base article. If tie, choose the first in search rank.
   - If none match from (a), take the top 3 titles from query (b) "Intermodal container" and repeat the same section-matching logic to select a base article.
   - Save: base_article.title and base_article.selected_from_query = either "Containerization" or "Intermodal container" depending on the query source.

3) Deep dive on base article (sequential; dependencies on selected base):
   - Call Wikipedia:get_article for the selected base article title.
   - Decision rule using article content: if the article text contains the exact substring "ISO 668" at least once, set a flag base_mentions_iso668 = true; otherwise false.
   - Call Wikipedia:summarize_article_section for the base with section_title = "History" and max_length = 150. If a "History" section does not exist, use the first available top-level section returned by Wikipedia:get_sections and note the section used.
   - Call Wikipedia:summarize_article_for_query on the base with query = "How standardization of intermodal containers affected shipping costs and logistics efficiency" and max_length = 250.
   - Call Wikipedia:extract_key_facts on the base with topic_within_article = "standardization" and count = 5.
   - Call Wikipedia:extract_key_facts on the base with topic_within_article = "economics" and count = 5.

4) Standards identification and cross-validation (iterative; conditional; dependencies on base):
   - Call Wikipedia:get_links on the base article. Filter linked titles to those whose title contains any of these substrings (case-insensitive): "ISO ", "IEC ", "standard", "ISO 668", "ISO 6346".
   - If fewer than 2 standards are found, then call Wikipedia:get_links on the title "Intermodal container" (if different from base) and merge the filtered links into the candidate set.
   - Construct an ordered list of up to 3 standard titles using the following priorities:
     Priority 1: If base_mentions_iso668 = true and "ISO 668" is in the candidate set, place "ISO 668" first.
     Priority 2: Include "ISO 6346" if present.
     Priority 3: Add any other link containing "ISO" or "standard" until you have at most 3 items.
   - For each selected standard title:
     a) Call Wikipedia:get_summary.
     b) Call Wikipedia:extract_key_facts with count = 3.
     c) Call Wikipedia:get_related_topics for the standard (limit = 10). Set cross_validated_with_base = true if either the base article title appears in the related topics OR the base article title appears in the base’s get_links result set and the standard title appears in the base’s get_links result set. Otherwise, set cross_validated_with_base = false.
     d) If cross_validated_with_base = false for any standard and there are more candidates available from the filtered links, replace the non-validated standard with the next available candidate and repeat steps a–c for that replacement. Stop when you have up to 3 standards or no more candidates.

5) Ports and global diffusion (iterative; branching; dependencies on base and related topics):
   - Call Wikipedia:get_related_topics on the base article with limit = 10. Combine these titles with the base’s get_links results.
   - Filter combined titles to those matching either of these patterns (case-insensitive): titles beginning with "Port of " or containing the substring "container port".
   - Select up to 5 unique port-related titles. If fewer than 3 are found, perform Wikipedia:search_wikipedia with query = "Container port" (limit = 5) and add any titles from that result that fit the patterns, until you have up to 5.
   - For each selected port title:
     a) Call Wikipedia:get_summary.
     b) Attempt Wikipedia:summarize_article_section with section_title = "History" and max_length = 150. If no such section exists, skip this sub-step and leave history_section_summary empty.
     c) Call Wikipedia:summarize_article_for_query with query = "role in the adoption of containerization" and max_length = 200.

6) Person profile (Malcom McLean) (sequential; fallback; dependencies on Step 1):
   - If a title exactly matching "Malcom McLean" exists in the results from query (c), use it. Otherwise, call Wikipedia:search_wikipedia with query = "Malcom McLean" (limit = 5) and take the top title that exactly matches or the closest match.
   - Call Wikipedia:get_summary for the chosen "Malcom McLean" title.
   - Call Wikipedia:extract_key_facts with topic_within_article = "container" and count = 5.

7) Relationship map (cross-link analysis; dependencies on selected items):
   - Build a node set consisting of: the base article, each selected standard, each selected port, and "Malcom McLean".
   - For each node in this set, call Wikipedia:get_links and check whether any other node title appears exactly in its links.
   - Construct an adjacency map where an edge exists from node A to node B if B’s exact title appears in A’s get_links results.

8) Assemble the final JSON report using the specified output format. Populate all fields. Use exact titles as returned by tools. Do not include any data not sourced from the tool outputs.

Completion criteria:
- All nine Wikipedia tools must be used as specified.
- Decision points and fallbacks must be followed and documented (e.g., which base article was selected and why, which standards were replaced due to failed cross-validation).
- The final report must include at least 1 base article, up to 3 standards (minimum 2 if possible), up to 5 ports (minimum 3 if possible), the Malcom McLean profile, and a non-empty relationship map.
- All summaries and facts must be derived from the called tools; do not invent content.
dependency_analysis:
Inherent tool dependencies and workflow patterns:
- Search → Section inspection → Selection: Wikipedia:search_wikipedia produces candidate titles. Wikipedia:get_sections inspects structure to choose the most suitable base article. This is a sequential, dependent chain where get_sections depends on search output.
- Full content → Targeted summaries: After selecting the base title, Wikipedia:get_article provides full text used for rule-based checks (e.g., presence of 'ISO 668'). Wikipedia:summarize_article_section and Wikipedia:summarize_article_for_query then create section-specific and query-specific condensations. Wikipedia:extract_key_facts further distills structured points. These tools (summarize and extract) depend on the chosen base and, for section summaries, on knowing section titles via get_sections.
- Link graph exploration: Wikipedia:get_links on the base article yields candidate standards and ports. Wikipedia:get_related_topics provides a complementary set of related entries, used both for candidate expansion and cross-validation. The selection of standards and ports depends on link/related topic outputs.

Scenario-based dependencies and decision logic:
- Base article selection decision: If none of the top 'Containerization' query candidates have sufficient target sections (History/Economics/Standards/Impact/Effects), the workflow falls back to 'Intermodal container' candidates. This creates a conditional branch based on get_sections outputs.
- Standards identification: The presence of the substring 'ISO 668' in the base article content (from get_article) elevates 'ISO 668' to priority 1 in the standards list. If fewer than two standards are found via base links, there is a fallback to use links from the 'Intermodal container' page. This enforces a dependency chain: get_article → content check → prioritization; get_links(base) → candidate pool; get_links(intermodal) → fallback expansion.
- Standards cross-validation: Each candidate standard undergoes Wikipedia:get_summary and Wikipedia:extract_key_facts for content extraction, and Wikipedia:get_related_topics to verify topical proximity to the base article. Additionally, cross-validation checks whether both the base and the standard appear in the base’s get_links result set, reinforcing associative relevance. If cross_validation fails and more candidates exist, the standard is replaced, creating an iterative loop.
- Ports selection and enrichment: Ports are discovered by combining Wikipedia:get_related_topics and Wikipedia:get_links for the base. If insufficient ports are found, Wikipedia:search_wikipedia with 'Container port' supplements the list. Each selected port then triggers Wikipedia:get_summary, Wikipedia:summarize_article_section (History), and Wikipedia:summarize_article_for_query tailored to 'role in the adoption of containerization', forming a dependent multi-tool enrichment chain.
- Person profile dependency: Uses initial search results for 'Malcom McLean' if available; otherwise falls back to a dedicated search. Subsequent Wikipedia:get_summary and Wikipedia:extract_key_facts depend on the selected person title.
- Relationship map construction: For the final set of nodes (base, standards, ports, person), Wikipedia:get_links is called for each to detect inter-node links, building an adjacency list. This stage depends on all previous selections and ensures a cross-validated network view.

Parallel vs sequential requirements:
- Sequential: Initial search and base selection (search → get_sections → decision), base deep-dive (get_article → summarizations → extract facts), and standards selection/cross-validation are largely sequential due to dependencies.
- Parallelizable segments: Once the base article is fixed and candidate lists are formed, enriching multiple standards and multiple ports can be executed in parallel (each standard/port item follows the same sequence of calls). However, iterative replacement of standards due to cross-validation failures introduces serial checks within the standards subset.

Cross-server dependencies:
- Not applicable in this task since all tools are on the single Wikipedia server. All inter-tool dependencies occur within the same server context.

Data flow summary:
- Titles from search_wikipedia feed into get_sections for filtering and into follow-on calls across the pipeline.
- The chosen base title parameterizes all subsequent base-centric calls (get_article, summarize_article_section, summarize_article_for_query, extract_key_facts, get_links, get_related_topics).
- Link and related-topic outputs condition the selection and ordering of standard and port pages, which then drive their summaries and fact extraction.
- Iterative standards cross-validation uses outputs from get_related_topics and get_links to enforce relevance, potentially cycling through candidates until constraints are met.
- The relationship map depends on the union of selected nodes, using get_links of each node to compute edges, which in turn validates and enriches the final report.

task_description:
Goal: Produce a rigorous, cross-validated intelligence brief on microfinance models, regulation, and controversies across Bangladesh, Kenya, Bolivia, India, and Peru using only the provided Wikipedia tools. The workflow must follow the dependency chain and decisions below, and the final output must be a structured report as specified.

Scope and concrete inputs:
- Seed search queries (limit 10 per query):
  - Microfinance
  - Microcredit
  - Grameen Bank
  - Kiva (organization)
  - M-Pesa
  - Mobile money
  - Credit union
  - BancoSol
  - Muhammad Yunus
  - Self-help group (finance)
  - Village savings and loan association
  - FINCA International
  - MiBanco
  - Kenya Women Microfinance Bank
  - Interest rate cap

Required tool sequence and decision logic:
1) Initial discovery (sequential):
   - For each seed query, call Wikipedia:search_wikipedia with limit=10.
   - From the returned titles, select the single most canonical article per query (e.g., exact or closest match by title). Document the mapping from query to chosen article title.

2) Baseline context (sequential on selected core concepts):
   - For the following selected articles (by their final titles), call Wikipedia:get_summary: Microfinance, Microcredit, Credit union, Village savings and loan association.

3) Organization controversy deep-dive (branching per article):
   - Target organization/implementation articles (by final titles): Grameen Bank, Kiva (organization), BancoSol, M-Pesa, FINCA International, MiBanco, Kenya Women Microfinance Bank.
   - For each, call Wikipedia:get_sections.
   - Decision A: If any section title contains one of ["Criticism", "Criticisms", "Controversy", "Controversies", "Debate"], then call Wikipedia:summarize_article_section with section_title set to that exact section title and max_length=200.
   - Decision B: If no such section exists, call Wikipedia:summarize_article_for_query with query="criticisms and controversies related to interest rates, consumer protection, and impact" and max_length=300.

4) Interest-rate/regulation extraction (sequential on the same article set):
   - For each of the core articles (Microfinance, Microcredit) and each organization article listed above, call Wikipedia:extract_key_facts with topic_within_article="interest rates and regulation" and count=5.
   - Additionally for Microfinance and Microcredit, call Wikipedia:summarize_article_for_query with query="regulatory frameworks by country and interest caps" and max_length=300.

5) Region case discovery via link mining (iterative with fallback):
   - Call Wikipedia:get_links on Microfinance and on Microcredit.
   - Filter the resulting link titles to identify region-relevant candidates per target region using the following match criteria:
     - Bangladesh: titles containing "Bangladesh", "Grameen Bank", "BRAC".
     - Kenya: titles containing "Kenya", "M-Pesa", "Kenya Women Microfinance Bank".
     - Bolivia: titles containing "Bolivia", "BancoSol".
     - India: titles containing "India", "Self-help group (finance)", "Bandhan Bank".
     - Peru: titles containing "Peru", "MiBanco".
   - Decision C (per region): If fewer than 1 candidate is found for a region from link mining, execute a fallback set of searches for that region with limit=10, in this exact order until at least one viable article title is found:
     - Bangladesh fallback queries: "microfinance Bangladesh", "BRAC", "Grameen Bank".
     - Kenya fallback queries: "microfinance Kenya", "M-Pesa", "Kenya Women Microfinance Bank".
     - Bolivia fallback queries: "microfinance Bolivia", "BancoSol".
     - India fallback queries: "microfinance India", "Self-help group (finance)", "Bandhan Bank".
     - Peru fallback queries: "microfinance Peru", "MiBanco".
   - Select exactly one article title per region as the region case article. If multiple are available, prefer the one that directly names a microfinance entity or mechanism over a general topic.

6) Region case extraction (sequential per selected region article):
   - For each selected region case article, call Wikipedia:get_summary.
   - Then call Wikipedia:extract_key_facts with topic_within_article="business model, regulation, interest rates, outreach" and count=5.
   - Then call Wikipedia:get_related_topics with limit=15. Decision D: If the related topics include a regulator or central bank (e.g., titles containing "Bank", "Central Bank", "regulator", or a named national authority), note it as the region regulator; else call Wikipedia:summarize_article_for_query on the region case article with query="regulation and oversight" and max_length=250 to extract oversight details textually.

7) Cross-article validation (dependent on prior extractions):
   - Construct at least two validation pairs: (Microfinance, Bangladesh case), (Microfinance, Kenya case). For each pair, call Wikipedia:extract_key_facts again if needed to ensure you have facts from both sides.
   - Decision E: A validation succeeds if the pair shares at least one consistent fact when compared by content (e.g., founder, country, mechanism name, or regulator reference). Record the overlapping fact text and the two article titles. If no overlap, record as "no match" and briefly hypothesize why (e.g., one article is too general or uses different terminology).

8) Concept map clustering (parallelizable after prior steps):
   - Call Wikipedia:get_related_topics for Microfinance (limit=15) and for Microcredit (limit=15).
   - Cluster the returned topics into four label groups based on title semantics: "Organizations", "Mechanisms/Models", "Regulators/Policies", "Controversies/Critiques". If an item fits multiple groups, choose the best-fit primary group and note any ambiguity.

Mandatory parameters for all tool calls:
- search_wikipedia.limit = 10 for all searches.
- summarize_article_section.max_length = 200 (as specified in step 3 when used).
- summarize_article_for_query.max_length = 300 unless otherwise specified.
- extract_key_facts.count = 5 unless otherwise specified; topic_within_article values exactly as given in steps 4 and 6.
- get_related_topics.limit = 15 when used in steps 6 and 8.

Output format (produce exactly these sections in order, using plain text and bullet lists where appropriate):
- Executive summary (<= 200 words) synthesizing what microfinance is, key mechanisms, and a high-level comparison across Bangladesh, Kenya, Bolivia, India, and Peru.
- Core definitions: 4–8 bullets summarizing Microfinance, Microcredit, Credit union, Village savings and loan association. Each bullet must end with the source article title in parentheses.
- Organization controversies: For each of Grameen Bank, Kiva (organization), BancoSol, M-Pesa, FINCA International, MiBanco, Kenya Women Microfinance Bank, provide 1 bullet with a 2–3 sentence controversy summary. End each bullet with the article title in parentheses.
- Region case insights: For each region (Bangladesh, Kenya, Bolivia, India, Peru), provide:
  - 1 bullet with the selected region case article title
  - 5 sub-bullets listing key facts (verbatim or close paraphrase) from extract_key_facts about business model, regulation, interest rates, and outreach.
- Regulatory overview by region: 1–3 bullets per region describing discovered or inferred regulators/oversight and any interest cap or notable regulatory mechanism. Cite the article title(s) used at the end of each bullet in parentheses.
- Cross-validation log: For each required pair, a bullet stating the two article titles, whether validation succeeded, and if so the overlapping fact. If not, state "no match" and a one-sentence hypothesis.
- Concept map description: 4 labeled bullet groups (Organizations; Mechanisms/Models; Regulators/Policies; Controversies/Critiques). Under each, list up to 5 of the most relevant related topics discovered, with the source root (Microfinance or Microcredit) in parentheses.
- Methodology log: Bullet list summarizing the tool calls made and all branch decisions at Decisions A–E, including any fallback searches per region and which article titles were ultimately selected.

Success criteria:
- All information is sourced solely via the specified Wikipedia tools in this task.
- Every required tool call, parameter, and decision branch is executed as specified.
- Each of the five target regions has exactly one selected case article with 5 key facts.
- Cross-validation pairs are attempted and logged with outcomes.
- The final output strictly follows the defined section order and content requirements.
dependency_analysis:
Inherent tool relationships:
- search_wikipedia -> get_article/get_summary/get_sections/get_links/get_related_topics/extract_key_facts/summarize_*: Initial discovery via search is needed to identify exact article titles before any downstream extraction or summarization.
- get_sections -> summarize_article_section: Section listing is a prerequisite to conditionally summarize specific sections (e.g., Criticism), establishing section-aware dependency.
- get_links and get_related_topics are complementary expansions: Links reveal within-article network targets; related_topics provides graph-based thematic neighbors. Both feed selection and clustering steps.
- extract_key_facts and summarize_article_for_query operate on known titles, so they depend on either search-derived or link-derived titles.

Scenario-based dependencies and decision points:
- Sequential core chain: (1) search_wikipedia (seed queries) -> (2) title selection -> (2) get_summary for core concepts -> (3) get_sections on org pages -> (3) Decision A/B to choose either summarize_article_section or summarize_article_for_query for controversies -> (4) extract_key_facts on interest/regulation for both core and org articles.
- Region discovery loop: (5) get_links on Microfinance and Microcredit -> filter per region -> Decision C per region. If the filter yields <1 candidate, fallback to targeted search_wikipedia with fixed regional queries until an article is found. This ensures coverage for all five regions through an iterative discover-and-fallback cycle.
- Region case extraction chain: (6) For each selected region article -> get_summary -> extract_key_facts (business model/regulation/interest/outreach) -> get_related_topics -> Decision D: If a regulator-like title appears in related topics, record it; else call summarize_article_for_query to extract regulatory/oversight detail textually.
- Cross-validation chain: (7) extract_key_facts on pairs (Microfinance, region case) -> Decision E: If any overlapping fact content exists (country, founder, mechanism, regulator), mark validation success and record; else mark no match with a hypothesis. This step enforces cross-article consistency checks.
- Concept map synthesis: (8) get_related_topics on Microfinance and Microcredit -> clustering into predefined semantic groups. This parallel step draws on earlier context but is independent of controversy/region flows, allowing concurrent execution after title acquisition.

Parallel vs sequential requirements:
- Sequential: Initial search, title selection, core summaries, section checks, and controversy summarizations must precede interest/regulation fact extraction to ensure correct scoping.
- Parallelizable: After titles are fixed, organization controversy processing across multiple org articles can proceed in parallel; likewise region case extraction per region can run in parallel once each region’s article is selected.
- Iterative loop: Region discovery includes an explicit loop with a threshold (>=1 candidate per region). If unmet from get_links, fallback search_wikipedia is triggered with predefined queries until the threshold is satisfied.

Data-driven parameterization:
- search results directly determine which article titles downstream tools consume. Section titles obtained from get_sections are used verbatim as inputs to summarize_article_section. Link titles and related topic outputs are filtered by concrete string criteria to determine regional relevance and regulator identification, respectively. The presence/absence of regulator-like related topics (Decision D) dictates whether to call summarize_article_for_query for oversight details.

Cross-validation and contradiction handling:
- Cross-article validation uses extract_key_facts on both a general concept (Microfinance) and a region case article, comparing content to confirm shared entities/facts. If no overlap is detected, the workflow mandates recording a "no match" with a hypothesized reason, capturing potential inconsistencies or granularity mismatches.

Server usage and constraints:
- All tools reside on the Wikipedia server; hence all dependencies are intra-server. Cross-source validation is simulated via cross-article comparisons and parallel use of get_links and get_related_topics to triangulate. No external servers or resources are used, satisfying the self-contained requirement.

Outcome dependency:
- The final structured report’s sections (definitions, controversies, region insights, regulatory overview, cross-validation log, concept map, methodology) cannot be populated without traversing the entire dependency graph: search to fix titles, sections for controversy branching, link/related topic expansions for region selection and clustering, and fact extraction for validation and regulatory synthesis.

task_description:
Goal: Produce a policy-oriented, evidence-backed comparative brief on mangrove conservation strategies for Indonesia, the Philippines, and Thailand using only the provided Wikipedia tools. Your output must be a single JSON object (structure specified below) built from iterative, conditional exploration and cross-validation across Wikipedia articles.

Topic scope and deliverables:
- Global context: Summarize ecosystem services and top threats to mangroves, plus 3–5 related global topics that inform policy (e.g., blue carbon, Ramsar Convention).
- Country analyses (Indonesia, Philippines, Thailand): For each country, identify and synthesize:
  - Threats (>=3 items)
  - Policy instruments/legislation/programs (>=2 items)
  - Restoration approaches (>=1 item)
  - Economic valuation or ecosystem service points (>=1 item)
- Validation:
  - At least two of each country’s threats must overlap with the global threat set; otherwise, flag a gap.
  - If a country has <2 policy instruments after first pass, trigger a second-pass link-based search for laws/acts.
- Evidence matrix: Log every extracted item with its Wikipedia article title and either section title or query used.

Strict data constraints:
- Use only the Wikipedia tools provided.
- Use the exact search terms and selection criteria below.
- No external sources, URLs, or outside data.

Execution plan and exact steps (including decision points and thresholds):
1) Seed the global baseline from the Mangrove article
   a. Fetch summary and sections for the article title: "Mangrove" using Wikipedia:get_summary and Wikipedia:get_sections.
   b. Attempt targeted section summaries using Wikipedia:summarize_article_section for each of these section_title candidates (call only if present): "Ecosystem services", "Threats", "Conservation", "Restoration". max_length: 150.
   c. If any of these sections are absent, call Wikipedia:summarize_article_for_query on title="Mangrove" with these queries (max_length: 250):
      - "ecosystem services of mangroves"
      - "threats to mangroves"
      - "mangrove conservation"
      - "mangrove restoration"
   d. Extract global key facts using Wikipedia:extract_key_facts with title="Mangrove":
      - topic_within_article="Ecosystem services", count=5
      - topic_within_article="Threats", count=5
   e. Save two global lists: global_top_threats (unique, up to 5) and global_ecosystem_services (unique, up to 5).

2) Expand global related context
   a. Call Wikipedia:get_related_topics on title="Mangrove", limit=15.
   b. From returned topics, select up to 5 that match any of these relevance keywords (case-insensitive substring match on title): ["blue carbon", "restoration", "Ramsar", "coastal management", "aquaculture", "mangrove deforestation", "protected area", "integrated coastal zone management", "ICZM"]. If more than 5 match, choose the first 5.
   c. For each selected related topic title:
      - Confirm relevance by calling Wikipedia:get_summary. If summary contains at least one of these tokens: ["mangrove", "coastal", "wetland", "conservation", "protection"], keep; otherwise discard and, if discarded, replace with the next candidate from step 2b.
      - Extract 3 key facts using Wikipedia:extract_key_facts with count=3.
   d. Save selected_related_topics (list of objects: {title, 1–2 sentence summary, key_facts[<=3]}).

3) Country-specific discovery (repeat for each country in ["Indonesia", "Philippines", "Thailand"]) – round 1
   a. Perform search queries using Wikipedia:search_wikipedia (limit=5 each):
      - "Mangroves in <Country>"
      - "<Country> mangroves"
      - "Mangrove conservation in <Country>"
      - "Environment of <Country>"
      - "Protected areas of <Country>"

dependency_analysis:
Inherent tool dependencies and chains:
- Discovery chain: Wikipedia:search_wikipedia → Wikipedia:get_summary (relevance screening) → Wikipedia:get_article/Wikipedia:get_sections (structure) → Wikipedia:summarize_article_section (targeted extraction). This is the primary sequential chain to move from discovery to detail.
- Fallback extraction: When a desired section is missing, Wikipedia:summarize_article_for_query consumes the article title and a specific query string, enabling targeted retrieval without section dependence.
- Fact distillation: Wikipedia:extract_key_facts operates on a known article title (optionally scoped by topic_within_article) to produce concise items used for validation and as seeds for additional queries.
- Topical expansion: Wikipedia:get_related_topics provides a candidate set of related pages; its output is subsequently screened via Wikipedia:get_summary and then mined via Wikipedia:extract_key_facts. This creates a multi-step dependency where related topic selection is conditional on summary token matches.
- Link mining: Wikipedia:get_links yields titles for potential policy/legislation/program pages, which are then processed through get_summary → get_sections → summarize_article_section / summarize_article_for_query. This constitutes a second discovery pipeline parallel to search-based discovery but triggered conditionally.

Scenario-based dependencies and decision points:
- Global-to-country dependency: The global_top_threats list (from extract_key_facts on "Mangrove") is used to validate and compare each country’s threat profile. Overlap thresholds (>=2) drive gap flags.
- Search selection logic: For each country, multiple fixed queries are issued. Titles are filtered by relevance tokens in get_summary output; only the first two relevant pages are selected, determining the subsequent extraction path.
- Section vs. query fallback: If targeted sections (e.g., "Policy", "Restoration") do not exist per get_sections, the agent must pivot to summarize_article_for_query on the same article with precise query strings. This conditional branch ensures progression without section reliance.
- Enrichment trigger: If minimum category thresholds (threats>=3, policy_instruments>=2, restoration>=1, economics>=1) are not met after round 1, the workflow triggers link mining (get_links) for up to 3 titles, followed by summary/section/query extraction. This creates an iterative refinement loop.
- Related-topic substitution: get_related_topics may return more than 5 relevant items; a filtering decision based on keyword presence in titles and token presence in summaries determines which are retained. Discarded topics are replaced iteratively from the candidate pool.

Parallel vs. sequential execution:
- Sequential: Within each article, the flow is strictly ordered: get_summary → get_sections → summarize_article_section and/or summarize_article_for_query. Similarly, the link-mining enrichment follows get_links → get_summary → get_sections → summarize calls.
- Parallel: Country workflows for Indonesia, Philippines, and Thailand can proceed in parallel, each executing the same sequential pipeline. Within each country, processing of the two selected pages can also be parallelized prior to integration.

Cross-server dependencies:
- Only the Wikipedia server is available; therefore, no cross-server dependencies apply. All cross-validation and enrichment occur within Wikipedia using different tools.

Data flow and transformation:
- Tokenization and filtering: get_summary outputs are scanned for inclusion tokens to ensure article relevance, thus shaping which titles proceed forward.
- Structured extraction: summarize_article_section and summarize_article_for_query outputs are transformed into categorized lists (threats, policy_instruments, restoration_approaches, economics_points) via keyword-informed parsing and de-duplication.
- Validation loop: extract_key_facts (global) → compare to country lists → if overlap deficiency or category count shortfall, trigger link-mining branch and re-aggregation.

Critical dependencies:
- Country-level completeness depends on both the availability of relevant sections and the success of query-based summarization; failure in either necessitates link-based enrichment.
- The evidence_matrix requires that every extracted item record its provenance; thus, section summarization or query summarization must be logged with the exact section title or query used, coupling extraction steps to the final reporting structure.

## Tool Dependency Analysis

### Key Tool Chains and Data Flow

**Chain 1: Discovery and Overview (Initial Research)**

2. **Section-Based Decision**: After `get_sections`, must determine which section titles contain 'Impact' or 'Effects' keywords for cross-validation

### Parallel vs Sequential Requirements

## Tool Dependency Analysis for Wikipedia Research Task

### A. INHERENT DEPENDENCIES (Natural Data Flow)

3. **Section-to-Detail Pipeline**:

4. **Related-Topic Exploration Pipeline**:

   - Creates iterative exploration loop

### B. SCENARIO-BASED DEPENDENCIES

1. **Decision Branch: Article Selection**

   - Different article choices lead to different subsequent data gathering

2. **Decision Branch: Related Topic Selection**

3. **Parallel vs Sequential Requirements**:
   - PARALLEL: After selecting primary article, extract_key_facts, get_sections, get_related_topics, get_links can all be called simultaneously (same title input)
   - SEQUENTIAL: get_sections output needed before summarize_article_section calls
   - SEQUENTIAL: Related topic exploration must wait for get_related_topics output

4. **Cross-Validation Pattern**:

   - summarize_article_for_query with specific queries provides targeted validation

5. **Iterative Refinement**:
   - Initial search → article selection → explore related topics → potentially return to search with new terms based on findings

### C. COMPLETE DEPENDENCY CHAIN

```
[search_wikipedia] → Extract titles
     ↓
[get_summary OR get_article] → Get primary article
     ↓
┌───────────────────────────────────────┐
│ PARALLEL CALLS (same title):          │
```

task_description: Objective: Build a comparative evidence-backed profile of four urban congestion pricing schemes using only Wikipedia tools, extract key impact metrics, cross-validate figures within each article, map shared related topics, and rank the schemes by reported first-year traffic reduction. Items to analyze (use these exact search queries): 1) "London congestion charge" 2) "Stockholm congestion tax" 3) "Electronic Road Pricing" (Singapore) 4) "Area C Milan" Required outputs: Produce a single consolidated result containing: - Per-city profile objects with fields: title (chosen article title), implementation_year, scheme_type (cordon/area/dynamic road pricing/other), primary_technology (e.g., ANPR cameras, RFID, gantry ERP), initial_charge_amount_local_currency (text as presented), reported_traffic_reduction_first_year_percent, emissions_reduction_first_year_percent (if available), public_acceptance_change_percent (if available), key_exemptions (up to 3 concise bullet points), data_confidence_notes (brief notes on any ambiguity or conflicting figures), sources_used (list of article titles used beyond the main article, if any). - Comparative ranking: an ordered list of the four schemes by reported_traffic_reduction_first_year_percent (descending). If ties, order by earlier implementation_year (earlier first). If still tied or unknown, order alphabetically by title. - Common related topics: up to 5 topic titles that appear in the get_related_topics results of at least two of the four main articles, listed by frequency (most frequent first; break ties alphabetically). Step-by-step required workflow (perform for each of the 4 queries, then do cross-article synthesis): A) Article discovery and selection (sequential): 1) Use Wikipedia:search_wikipedia with the specified query and limit=5. 2) Selection rule: If an exact title match to the prominent scheme is present (e.g., "London congestion charge", "Stockholm congestion tax", "Electronic Road Pricing", "Area C (Milan)"), choose it. Else choose the first result. Record chosen title. 3) Fetch the full article using Wikipedia:get_article for the chosen title. B) Section discovery and targeted summaries (sequential with decisions): 4) Use Wikipedia:get_sections on the chosen title. Identify the highest-priority section, in this order, to capture impact outcomes: Impact > Effects > Results > Evaluation > Reception. If none of these exist, skip to step 7. 5) Use Wikipedia:summarize_article_section on the chosen title and the identified section_title with max_length=250 to capture impact-outcome details. 6) Use Wikipedia:extract_key_facts with title set to the chosen article and topic_within_article="impact" and count=7 to pull candidate numeric facts (e.g., percent traffic and emissions changes, date markers). 7) Use Wikipedia:summarize_article_for_query on the chosen title with a composite query string: "traffic reduction percent first year; emissions reduction percent first year; implementation year; initial charge; exemptions; technology (ANPR, ERP, RFID)" and max_length=250. If traffic reduction percent is still absent, run a second Wikipedia:summarize_article_for_query with query="traffic reduction percent initial implementation" and max_length=200. C) Extract technology, exemptions, and acceptance (sequential with fallbacks): 8) Technology: If primary_technology is not clearly indicated from steps 5–7, run Wikipedia:summarize_article_for_query again with query="technology used detection method ANPR RFID ERP smartcard camera gantry" and max_length=200. 9) Exemptions: If exemptions are unclear from steps 5–7, use Wikipedia:get_links on the chosen title, then scan the returned link titles for terms containing any of: exemption, resident, discount, low emission, blue badge, taxi. For up to two of the most relevant-looking links, fetch Wikipedia:get_summary and extract concise exemption details (only keep content that clearly describes scheme exemptions/discounts). Add the linked titles to sources_used. 10) Public acceptance: Within the section list from step 4, if a section contains any of: Public opinion, Referendum, Evaluation, Poll, then run Wikipedia:summarize_article_section (max_length=200) for that section and capture any percent change in public acceptance from before to after implementation. If no such section exists, use Wikipedia:get_related_topics (limit=15) and select any related topic title containing referendum or opinion; if found, fetch Wikipedia:get_summary on that topic and extract acceptance figures (if any). Add any such related-topic titles consulted to sources_used. D) Resolve key metrics with decision rules (sequential decisions): 11) implementation_year: Prefer an explicit year from the lead sentence via Wikipedia:get_summary. If ambiguous or conflicting with extract_key_facts, prefer the year in the lead. If still ambiguous, choose the earliest year explicitly tied to the scheme’s start (not to pilot studies unless the article states the pilot as the formal start). 12) reported_traffic_reduction_first_year_percent: If multiple candidate percentages are found, prefer the one explicitly labeled as within the first year after introduction. If no first-year label, prefer the value associated with the shortest time window post-introduction (e.g., first month) only if the article describes it as representative of initial impact; otherwise mark unknown. 13) emissions_reduction_first_year_percent: Extract if explicitly provided for the first year; otherwise leave unknown. 14) initial_charge_amount_local_currency: Prefer the earliest charge cited at introduction (not later increases); if both introduction and later increases are present, record only the introduction figure and note differences in data_confidence_notes. 15) scheme_type: Classify based on article evidence: cordon (charges for crossing a boundary), area (charges for presence within a zone), dynamic road pricing (charges vary in real-time by location/time), or other (briefly describe). 16) primary_technology: Select one term that best characterizes detection/payment tech, e.g., ANPR cameras, ERP gantries, RFID transponders, smartcards. E) Related topics intersection (cross-article synthesis): 17) For each of the four main articles, run Wikipedia:get_related_topics with limit=12. 18) Construct a frequency map of returned topic titles; include only topics that appear in at least two of the four lists. Sort by frequency (desc), then alphabetically; keep up to 5. F) Ranking (cross-article synthesis): 19) Rank the four schemes by reported_traffic_reduction_first_year_percent (desc). Ties: earliest implementation_year first, remaining ties alphabetical by title. G) Final deliverable structure: Output a single structure containing: - profiles: array of 4 objects (one per scheme) with all fields listed above - ranking: ordered array of the four chosen titles - common_related_topics: ordered array of up to 5 topic titles - methodology_notes: brief notes indicating which sections and queries produced each key metric, and any unresolved ambiguities (1–2 sentences per scheme). Do not use any external sources beyond the specified Wikipedia tools. Use only the concrete queries and tool parameters defined above. If any field cannot be confidently determined after executing all fallbacks, set it to "unknown" and explain in data_confidence_notes.
dependency_analysis: Inherent tool dependencies (Wikipedia server only): - search_wikipedia → get_article/get_summary/get_sections: Search determines which article title to fetch and analyze. - get_sections → summarize_article_section: Section enumeration is required before targeted section summarization. - get_article/get_summary/extract_key_facts/summarize_article_for_query: These tools complement each other to surface both structured facts and narrative details; outputs cross-validate each other. - get_links/get_related_topics → get_summary/get_article: Link and related-topic discovery inform subsequent fetches for exemptions and public acceptance context. Scenario-based dependencies and data flow: 1) Discovery chain (sequential): search_wikipedia returns candidate titles; selection logic picks the canonical scheme article; then get_article provides full content; get_sections enumerates structure for downstream targeted summarization. 2) Impact extraction (sequential with decision points and iteration): - Decision point A: If an Impact (or fallback) section exists (from get_sections), then summarize_article_section is invoked; otherwise, skip to whole-article query summarization. - Decision point B: If summarize_article_section and extract_key_facts disagree on the implementation year, prefer get_summary’s lead; if still ambiguous, choose earliest year tied to formal start. - Iterative loop: If traffic reduction percent is missing after the first section summary, run summarize_article_for_query with targeted queries; if still missing, run a refined query; if still unresolved, mark unknown and note ambiguity. 3) Technology and exemptions (sequential with fallbacks): - Technology: If not found via initial summaries, trigger another summarize_article_for_query focused on detection/payment tech keywords (ANPR, ERP, RFID, gantry). - Exemptions: If initial sources lack clarity, get_links provides candidate linked titles; decision point C filters for relevant links (exemption/resident/discount/low emission), then get_summary on these links supplies supplementation. 4) Public acceptance (branching): - If a relevant section is present (Public opinion/Referendum/Evaluation), summarize it; else branch to get_related_topics and pick any topic including referendum/opinion; fetch its summary for acceptance metrics. This is a conditional workflow driven by section presence. 5) Cross-validation (within-server): - implementation_year is validated by comparing extract_key_facts and section summary against get_summary (lead). - traffic and emissions percentages are reconciled by preferring those explicitly tied to the first year; otherwise results are considered ambiguous. 6) Parallelization vs sequentiality: - Per-city pipelines are sequential internally (discovery → sections → summaries → key facts → links/related topics fallbacks). - Across the four cities, pipelines can run in parallel; however, the E) related-topics intersection requires aggregation after all four get_related_topics calls complete. 7) Aggregation and ranking (synthesis): - After per-city extraction, a cross-article frequency map of related topics is computed; topics appearing in at least two cities are retained. - Ranking depends on the resolved reported_traffic_reduction_first_year_percent; tie-breakers rely on implementation_year, which in turn depends on earlier cross-validation steps. 8) Error handling and completeness: - If any metric remains undetermined after all fallbacks (section summary → query summary → key facts → related/linked summaries), the value is set to "unknown" with an explanatory note in data_confidence_notes. Cross-server considerations: - Only the Wikipedia server is available; thus, cross-server validation is not applicable. Instead, cross-tool validation within the same server is mandated (lead summary vs section summaries vs key facts vs tailored query summaries) to minimize reliance on any single extraction method. Critical decision points summarized: - Title selection from search results (exact match vs first result). - Impact section presence determines whether to use section-level summarization or fall back to article-level query summarization. - Conflicting figures resolved by explicit first-year labeling and lead-summary precedence for start year. - Missing exemptions/acceptance triggers link/related-topic exploration. - Final ranking depends on successfully extracted percentages; tie-breakers depend on validated implementation years. The task enforces deep, multi-step dependencies and iterative refinement requiring many tool calls across search, structural analysis, targeted summarization, fact extraction, link traversal, and cross-article synthesis.
