task_description:
Goal: Produce a comparative, cross-validated management briefing on three karst landscapes—South China Karst, The Burren, and Carlsbad Caverns National Park—using only the provided Wikipedia tools. The briefing must synthesize geology, conservation/management practices, visitor impacts, and common vs. site-specific strategies, validated against the general "Karst" article and, if needed, the general articles "Protected area" and "Visitor management". All thresholds, titles, queries, and limits are specified below.

Targets (exact primary article titles to seek):
- South China Karst
- The Burren
- Carlsbad Caverns National Park
- Karst (general reference)
Fallback/general support articles (only if triggered by conditions):
- Protected area
- Visitor management

Exact queries (use these in search_wikipedia):
- "South China Karst"
- "The Burren"
- "Carlsbad Caverns National Park"
- "Karst"
- "Protected area" (only if triggered)
- "Visitor management" (only if triggered)

Section-targeting keywords (case-insensitive):
- Geology section match set: ["Geology", "Geomorphology", "Geographical setting", "Formation", "Geography"]
- Management/conservation section match set: ["Conservation", "Management", "Protection", "Environmental issues", "Preservation"]
- Visitor/tourism section match set: ["Tourism", "Visitor", "Visitation", "Public access"]

Strategy keyword substrings for link filtering (case-insensitive):
["UNESCO", "World Heritage", "National Park Service", "protected", "buffer", "reforestation", "water", "pollution", "visitor", "access", "habitat", "endemic", "speleothem", "limestone", "karst", "cave"]

Execution plan (must follow the sequence and decision points):
1) Discovery and selection (per target article):
   a. Call Wikipedia:search_wikipedia with the corresponding query (limit=5). Choose the result whose title exactly matches the target title. If no exact match appears in the top 5, choose the first result that contains the distinctive target words (e.g., for South China Karst: must contain both "South" and "Karst"; for The Burren: must contain "Burren"; for Carlsbad Caverns: must contain "Carlsbad" and "Caverns").
   b. Call Wikipedia:get_summary on the chosen title to verify relevance (ensure the summary references karst or cave context for all three sites and a general karst context for "Karst"). If the summary appears unrelated to karst/caves, return to step 1a and pick the next search result.

2) Section mapping (per selected article):
   a. Call Wikipedia:get_sections. From the returned section titles, identify:
      - geology_section: first section matching any of the Geology keywords
      - management_section: first section matching any of the Management/conservation keywords
      - visitor_section: first section matching any of the Visitor/tourism keywords
   b. If none of the above are found for a given category (e.g., no management_section), note it as missing for decision steps below.

3) Targeted summarization (per selected article):
   a. Geology: If geology_section exists, call Wikipedia:summarize_article_section with max_length=150. Otherwise, call Wikipedia:summarize_article_for_query with query="geology geomorphology formation rock types hydrology" and max_length=180.
   b. Management/conservation: If management_section exists, call Wikipedia:summarize_article_section with max_length=180. Otherwise, call Wikipedia:summarize_article_for_query with query="conservation management environmental protection threats mitigation UNESCO management plan visitor impact" and max_length=180.
   c. Visitor impacts: If visitor_section exists, call Wikipedia:summarize_article_section with max_length=120. Otherwise, call Wikipedia:summarize_article_for_query with query="tourism visitor impacts access restrictions infrastructure carrying capacity" and max_length=150.

4) Key fact extraction (per selected article):
   a. Call Wikipedia:extract_key_facts with topic_within_article="Geology" and count=5.
   b. Call Wikipedia:extract_key_facts with topic_within_article="Conservation" and count=5.

5) Link and related-topic harvesting (per selected article):
   a. Call Wikipedia:get_links; filter returned links by the strategy keyword substrings list; keep up to 10 filtered links (or as many as available if fewer than 10 match). Record the filtered set as management_links.
   b. Call Wikipedia:get_related_topics with limit=10. Record the list.

6) General karst cross-reference:
   a. For the general "Karst" article, repeat steps 2 and 3 using the same keywords. If no management/conservation-like section is found, call Wikipedia:summarize_article_for_query with query="threats to karst landscapes conservation best practices management hydrology pollution" and max_length=220.
   b. Call Wikipedia:extract_key_facts on "Karst" with topic_within_article="Conservation" and count=7.
   c. Call Wikipedia:get_links on "Karst"; filter links using the strategy keyword substrings; keep up to 12.
   d. Call Wikipedia:get_related_topics on "Karst" with limit=12.

7) Sparsity fallback for site-specific management:
   a. For any site where either (i) no management_section was found AND the management_summary (from 3b) is under 50 words OR (ii) management_links filtered in step 5a are fewer than 3, perform both:
      - Call Wikipedia:search_wikipedia for "Protected area" (limit=3), choose the result titled exactly "Protected area"; call Wikipedia:summarize_article_for_query with query="management strategies visitor impact enforcement buffer zones" and max_length=160.
      - Call Wikipedia:search_wikipedia for "Visitor management" (limit=3), choose the result titled exactly "Visitor management"; call Wikipedia:summarize_article_for_query with query="visitor impact mitigation carrying capacity zoning closures education" and max_length=160.
   b. Use these two summaries to supplement missing management strategy elements for that site.

8) Content validation with full article (conditional):
   a. For any site where none of the three sections (geology, management, visitor) were found in step 2, call Wikipedia:get_article on that site and scan the full content text for the substrings "geol" (to catch geology variants), "conserv"/"manag"/"protect", and "tour"/"visitor". If any are found, retry step 2b using the exact section titles as they appear in the full content; if still missing, keep the query-based summaries from step 3.

9) Cross-site synthesis and validation:
   a. Build a set of strategy terms for each site by combining:
      - tokens/phrases appearing in the management_summary
      - the filtered management_links titles
      - the related topics list
   b. Validate each site’s strategy terms against the general "Karst" article by checking overlap with either (i) the filtered links of "Karst" or (ii) the "Karst" related topics. Mark a site’s strategy term as "validated" if it appears in either set; otherwise mark it "site-specific".
   c. Construct a commonality/difference analysis: identify strategies that are validated and shared by at least 2 sites; identify strategies unique to one site.

10) Output format (return a single JSON object with this exact structure):
{

    },
    {

      "visitor_impacts_summary": "<=150 words",
      "key_facts_geology": ["5 items"],

      "related_topics": ["10 items"],
      "strategy_terms": ["derived terms (<=12)"],
      "sparsity_fallback_used": true/false
    }
  ],
  "general_karst": {
    "article_title": "Karst",
    "management_or_threats_summary": "<=220 words",
    "key_facts_conservation": ["7 items"],
    "filtered_links": ["<=12 link titles"],
    "related_topics": ["12 items"]
  },
  "cross_site_analysis": {
    "validated_common_strategies": ["strategies present in >=2 sites and validated by the Karst article (<=10)"],
    "site_specific_strategies": {
      "South China Karst": ["<=8"],
      "The Burren": ["<=8"],
      "Carlsbad Caverns National Park": ["<=8"]
    },
    "noted_threats_matrix": [
      {"site": "South China Karst", "threats": ["<=6"]},
      {"site": "The Burren", "threats": ["<=6"]},
      {"site": "Carlsbad Caverns National Park", "threats": ["<=6"]}
    ],

}

Notes:
- All tool limits and max_length parameters are fixed as above.
- Perform steps 1–5 for each site; step 6 once for "Karst"; step 7 only if triggered; step 8 only if all three sections absent for a site.
- Ensure decision criteria are applied exactly to trigger fallbacks and validations.

dependency_analysis:
Inherent tool chains and data flow:
- Discovery chain: Wikipedia:search_wikipedia → Wikipedia:get_summary → (validate relevance) → proceed with selected title. The search output determines the exact article title to use for all subsequent calls.
- Structural mapping chain: Wikipedia:get_sections provides the authoritative section title strings required by Wikipedia:summarize_article_section. Without get_sections, section summarization cannot target the correct headings.
- Content extraction chain: After title selection, Wikipedia:extract_key_facts, Wikipedia:get_links, and Wikipedia:get_related_topics all depend on the confirmed article title. Their outputs feed downstream filtering and validation.
- Tailored summarization chain: If a target section exists, Wikipedia:summarize_article_section is used; otherwise, Wikipedia:summarize_article_for_query with explicit queries fills the gap. This enforces a dependency on the get_sections result to choose which summarization tool is appropriate.

Scenario-based dependencies and decision points:
- Selection decision: From Wikipedia:search_wikipedia results, Wikipedia:get_summary is required to validate article relevance; only after confirmation is the title fixed for subsequent tools.
- Section-dependent branching: Presence or absence of geology/management/visitor sections (from Wikipedia:get_sections) dictates whether to call Wikipedia:summarize_article_section (section present) or Wikipedia:summarize_article_for_query (section absent). This creates a critical branching point per category.
- Sparsity fallback trigger: If management content is sparse (no section and summary under 50 words, or fewer than 3 filtered management links from Wikipedia:get_links), then additional searches for "Protected area" and "Visitor management" are performed, followed by Wikipedia:summarize_article_for_query on those articles to supplement strategies. This creates a deep, conditional dependency path extending beyond the primary site article.
- Full-content rescue: If all three target sections are missing for a site, Wikipedia:get_article is invoked to inspect raw content and potentially re-identify section titles for a retry with Wikipedia:get_sections and Wikipedia:summarize_article_section. This is an iterative loop with a fallback to query-based summaries if section discovery still fails.
- Validation against general reference: Strategy terms derived from site-level management summaries, filtered links (Wikipedia:get_links), and related topics (Wikipedia:get_related_topics) are cross-validated against the general "Karst" article using its filtered links and related topics. This requires prior completion of the general article pipeline (Wikipedia:get_sections → targeted summaries/Wikipedia:summarize_article_for_query → Wikipedia:extract_key_facts → Wikipedia:get_links → Wikipedia:get_related_topics). The validation step thus has a dependency on both site-level and general-article-level data.

Parallel vs. sequential requirements:
- Parallelizable: Steps 1–5 can be run in parallel for the three site articles once their titles are confirmed. However, each site’s workflow is internally sequential due to branching decisions based on prior outputs (e.g., get_sections before choosing the summary tool).
- Sequential constraints: The general "Karst" analysis (step 6) must be completed before cross-site validation (step 9). Sparsity fallbacks (step 7) are only evaluated after link filtering and management summarization have been completed for each site. Full-content rescue (step 8) is invoked only after section discovery fails entirely.

Cross-server dependencies:
- Only a single server (Wikipedia) is available. Therefore, there are no cross-server dependencies. All validation and fallback operations occur within the Wikipedia server using distinct articles as sources.

Data transformation and combination:
- Link filtering uses a predefined keyword list to transform Wikipedia:get_links outputs into a management_links subset. Strategy_terms are then synthesized by combining tokens from management summaries, filtered links, and related topics. Cross-validation transforms these terms by marking them as validated or site-specific based on overlap with the general "Karst" article’s links/related topics.

Iterative loops and re-analysis:
- The full-content rescue loop (step 8) prompts re-analysis of sections after inspecting full article text from Wikipedia:get_article. The sparsity fallback loop (step 7) augments missing management content with general strategies and feeds back into the strategy_terms construction prior to cross-site validation.

Overall, the task forces the agent to orchestrate a multi-branch pipeline where outputs of search, section discovery, and content extraction govern which summarization and fallback tools to call, culminating in a cross-validated synthesis that cannot be produced without understanding and executing the dependencies across the Wikipedia toolset.

task_description:
You are an AI research assistant for a materials science startup developing advanced dry adhesives. Your task is to compile a comprehensive biomimetic design brief on 'Gecko adhesion' and 'Synthetic setae'. You must solely use the provided Wikipedia tools to research the biological mechanisms, physical forces, and engineering applications of this technology. Execute the following steps in order:

1. Initial Discovery: Use the Wikipedia search tool to find the exact article titles for 'Gecko' and 'Synthetic setae'.
2. Biological Mechanism: Retrieve the sections of the 'Gecko' article. Identify the specific section that discusses their feet, toes, or adhesion capabilities. Use the section summarization tool to extract a summary of this specific section (max 200 words).
3. Physics Validation: Search for the fundamental physical force responsible for this adhesion (Van der Waals forces). Retrieve the article summary for this force to establish the scientific baseline.
4. Engineering & Biomimetics: For the 'Synthetic setae' article (or closest matching title found in Step 1), extract exactly 7 key facts specifically focused on the topic 'manufacturing methods and materials used'.
5. Cross-Topic Exploration: Get the related topics for the 'Synthetic setae' article. Identify exactly two related articles that pertain to robotics, climbing, or general biomimetics. 
6. Targeted Application Extraction: For the two related articles identified in Step 5, use the query-based summarization tool to extract information specifically about 'applications in climbing robots or space exploration' (max length 250 words each).
7. Synthesis: Combine all gathered information into a structured 'Biomimetic Adhesive Design Brief' containing:
   - Part A: Biological & Physical Foundations (combining the gecko section summary and the physics summary).
   - Part B: Material Engineering (listing the 7 extracted manufacturing facts).
   - Part C: Advanced Applications (synthesizing the robotic/space applications from the related topics).

Do not ask for further input. If a specific section title is not obvious, use your best judgment to select the closest matching section based on the list provided by the sections tool.
dependency_analysis: The task enforces a deep, multi-branch dependency chain utilizing almost all available Wikipedia tools in a strict sequence. 1. Discovery Dependency: `search_wikipedia` dictates the exact exact string titles passed to all subsequent tools. 2. Structural Dependency: `get_sections` output is inherently required as an input parameter (`section_title`) for `summarize_article_section`. 3. Branching & Filtering: The output of `get_related_topics` acts as a dynamic decision point; the agent must filter the returned list to select two relevant articles before passing them into `summarize_article_for_query`. 4. Specialized Extraction: `extract_key_facts` must be parameterized with a specific topical focus derived from the prompt, running in parallel to the section summaries. The final synthesis requires the agent to hold states from Step 2 (biology), Step 3 (physics), Step 4 (manufacturing), and Step 6 (applications) to generate a cohesive report, effectively cross-validating biological phenomena with physics and engineering applications.

1. INITIAL RESEARCH: Search Wikipedia for articles related to 'Apollo program' to identify the primary article and related topics. From the search results, identify the exact Wikipedia article title for the Apollo program.

2. ARTICLE RETRIEVAL: Using the exact article title from step 1, fetch:
   - The full article content
   - The list of sections
   - Extract 10 key facts from the article

3. RELATED TOPICS EXPLORATION: Use 'get_related_topics' with the Apollo program article title to discover at least 8 related topics. For each related topic, retrieve a summary.

4. DECISION POINT - INVESTIGATION PATH: Based on the extracted key facts and related topics, identify which Apollo mission had the most significant impact. You must justify your choice using specific facts from the extracted data. Then fetch the Wikipedia article for that mission.

5. MISSION-SPECIFIC DEEP DIVE: For your chosen mission:
   - Extract 5 key facts about the mission
   - Get sections and summarize the most important section
   - Get related topics for the mission

6. CROSS-VALIDATION: Use 'summarize_article_for_query' twice:
   - First query: "What were the scientific experiments conducted?"
   - Second query: "What was the cost and budget impact?"
   
7. TECHNOLOGY LEGACY: Use 'get_links' on the Apollo program article to identify technological links. Then search Wikipedia for 'Space Shuttle' and 'International Space Station' articles.

8. COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS: Fetch summaries for both Space Shuttle and International Space Station articles, then extract 3 key facts from each.

9. IMPACT ASSESSMENT: Combine all gathered information to create a comprehensive report with these exact sections:
   - Executive Summary (150 words max)
   - Apollo Program Overview (based on key facts)
   - Most Significant Mission Analysis (with justification)
   - Scientific Contributions (from cross-validation queries)
   - Technological Legacy Chain (how Apollo led to Space Shuttle to ISS)
   - Key Statistics Comparison Table

10. VALIDATION: List any contradictions or discrepancies found between different tool outputs (e.g., between get_summary vs get_article, or between extract_key_facts and summarize_article_for_query).

All findings must reference specific sources from the Wikipedia data you retrieved. Your final report must demonstrate clear data lineage - every claim must be traceable to a specific tool output.

task_description:
For an upcoming oceanography symposium this week, compile a highly detailed comparative technical and historical report on three pivotal crewed deep-sea submersibles: the bathyscaphe operated by Jacques Piccard in 1960, the DSV used extensively for Titanic wreck exploration, and the vessel piloted by James Cameron in 2012. You must strictly follow this investigative workflow using Wikipedia tools: 

1. Search and Identify: Use `search_wikipedia` to find the exact Wikipedia article titles for these three specific vessels. 
2. Section Mapping: Once you have the exact article titles, use `get_sections` for each of the three submersibles. 
3. Targeted Summarization: Based on the section lists, identify the section(s) discussing the vessel's 'Design', 'Specifications', or 'Development'. Use `summarize_article_section` (with max_length 200) on these specific sections to extract details about their hull materials, pressure resistance, and life support systems. 
4. Fact Extraction: Use `extract_key_facts` to gather exactly 5 facts per vessel. Set the `topic_within_article` parameter to 'Challenger Deep' for the Piccard and Cameron vessels, and 'Titanic wreck' for the third vessel, to retrieve the exact dates, depths reached, and key milestones. 
5. Contextual Expansion: Search for the article on 'Challenger Deep'. Use `get_related_topics` (limit 15) on the 'Challenger Deep' article. Review the returned related topics and use `get_summary` ONLY for related topics that represent a geographic trench, tectonic plate, or oceanographic zone (skip biographical or corporate entities). 
6. Final Synthesis: Combine your findings into a structured Markdown report featuring: 
- A comparative table of the three submersibles (Vessel Name, Key Technical Design, Milestone Event Date, Max Depth). 
- A detailed breakdown of their engineering evolution based on the section summaries. 
- A geographic context section describing the Challenger Deep and its related geographic/oceanographic features based on your contextual expansion research.
dependency_analysis: This task requires deep, multi-layered sequential tool chains and conditional logic. 1) Discovery dependency: `search_wikipedia` must successfully run to yield the exact canonical article titles for the three submersibles before any further analysis can begin. 2) Structural dependency: `get_sections` takes the titles from step 1 to output the table of contents. The agent must parse this output to dynamically determine the exact section headings (which vary between articles, e.g., 'Design' vs 'Specifications'). 3) Targeted extraction dependency: `summarize_article_section` uses the titles from step 1 and the exact section names from step 2. 4) Parameterized extraction: `extract_key_facts` requires setting the `topic_within_article` conditionally based on the vessel's historical context (Challenger Deep vs Titanic). 5) Exploratory branching: `get_related_topics` outputs an array of entities, forcing a decision point where the agent must evaluate the semantic nature of each related topic (filtering out people/companies) and conditionally route only geographic/oceanographic features into `get_summary`. 6) Final synthesis: Requires aggregating highly heterogeneous data formats (lists of facts, section summaries, related topic summaries) into a unified comparative schema.

task_description:
You are an expert researcher. Your task is to investigate the Chicxulub impact, its immediate environmental effects, the subsequent mass extinction, and the recovery of life. Follow these exact steps sequentially and conditionally:

1. Use `search_wikipedia` with the query "Chicxulub crater" to find the exact article title.
2. Use `extract_key_facts` on the Chicxulub crater article with `topic_within_article` set to "impact energy and physical characteristics of the crater" and `count` set to 5.
3. Use `get_sections` on the Chicxulub crater article. Identify the section that discusses environmental or climate effects (e.g., "Environmental effects", "Climate change", or similar). Use `summarize_article_section` to summarize this specific section with `max_length` 250.
4. Use `search_wikipedia` with the query "Cretaceous-Paleogene extinction event" to find the exact article title for the mass extinction event.
5. Use `get_sections` on the extinction event article. You need to analyze the impact on two specific groups: Mammals and Birds. Inspect the output to check if there are distinct sections dedicated specifically to these groups (they might be named "Mammals", "Birds", "Avian dinosaurs", or similar).
6. DECISION BRANCH:
   - If distinct sections for Mammals and Birds exist in the article, use `summarize_article_section` for each of them with `max_length` 200.
   - If distinct sections DO NOT exist, use `summarize_article_for_query` on the extinction event article twice, using the queries "What was the impact of the extinction event on mammals?" and "What was the impact of the extinction event on birds?", setting `max_length` to 200 for each.
7. Use `search_wikipedia` with the query "Cenozoic" to find the main article about the geological era following the extinction.
8. Use `summarize_article_for_query` on the "Cenozoic" article with the query "How did flora and fauna recover and diversify after the Cretaceous-Paleogene extinction?" and `max_length` 300.
9. Compile your findings into a comprehensive structured report containing:
   - Impact Characteristics: The 5 key facts about the Chicxulub crater.
   - Environmental Changes: The section summary of the crater's environmental effects.
   - Extinction Analysis: The analysis of how mammals and birds fared, based on either the section summaries or query summaries from Step 6.
   - Era of Recovery: The query-based summary of life's recovery in the Cenozoic era.
dependency_analysis:
This task features deep inherent and scenario-based dependency chains within the Wikipedia server. 

Key Tool Chains & Data Flow:
1. Search-to-Extraction: `search_wikipedia` provides the exact canonical title required by all subsequent data extraction tools (`extract_key_facts`, `get_sections`, `summarize_article_for_query`).
2. Section Discovery-to-Targeted Summarization: `get_sections` outputs an array of structural headers, which serves as the required input parameter (`section_title`) for `summarize_article_section`.

Critical Decision Points:
- Step 6 introduces a conditional workflow requiring dynamic evaluation of intermediate tool outputs. The agent must parse the section list of the extinction article. If specific string matches (or close semantic matches) for Mammals/Birds exist, the agent routes execution to `summarize_article_section`. If not, it falls back to an alternative strategy using `summarize_article_for_query`. This prevents blind linear execution and tests adaptive tool usage.

Parallel vs Sequential Requirements:
- Sequential: Searching for an article must strictly precede retrieving its sections or summarizing it. Discovering sections must strictly precede the conditional branch evaluation.
- Parallel: Once the exact titles are found, the parallel investigations into the Chicxulub crater (facts and sections), the K-Pg extinction event, and the Cenozoic era can be executed concurrently. The dual queries or section summaries for Mammals and Birds can also be fired in parallel once the condition is evaluated.

task_description:
I'm researching the history and science of anesthesia for a medical history presentation. I need a comprehensive, structured report covering the following:

1. **Discovery and Early History**: Start by searching Wikipedia for 'history of anesthesia' and related terms. Identify the key Wikipedia article(s) on this topic. Get the full article on 'Anesthesia' and also retrieve its section list. Then summarize the 'History' section (or equivalent) of the main anesthesia article.

2. **Key Figures Investigation**: From the main anesthesia article, extract key facts focused on 'pioneers and key figures in anesthesia'. Then, for EACH of the top 3 individuals mentioned (e.g., Crawford Long, William Morton, Horace Wells, or whoever appears), do the following:
   a. Search Wikipedia for that person's name.
   b. Get a summary of their Wikipedia article.
   c. Extract 5 key facts from their article focused on 'contributions to anesthesia'.
   d. Get related topics from their article to identify any cross-connections between the pioneers.

3. **Types of Anesthesia**: From the section list of the main 'Anesthesia' article, identify sections about types/classifications of anesthesia (e.g., general anesthesia, local anesthesia, regional anesthesia). Summarize each of these sections. Then get the full articles for 'General anaesthesia' and 'Local anesthesia', extract 5 key facts from each, and compare them.

4. **Key Substances**: Search for 'ether anesthesia', 'chloroform anesthesia', and 'nitrous oxide anesthesia'. For each substance found, get a tailored summary of its Wikipedia article focused on 'use as an anesthetic agent and historical significance'. Also extract key facts from each article focused on 'medical use and risks'.

5. **Modern Developments**: From the main anesthesia article, get related topics (limit 15). Identify any related topics that deal with modern anesthetic drugs or techniques. For up to 3 of these modern topics, retrieve their summaries and extract key facts.

6. **Cross-Validation**: Compare the historical timeline information from the main anesthesia History section summary with the biographical dates and claims from the individual pioneer articles. Note any discrepancies or complementary details.

**Final Output Format**: Provide a structured report with these sections:
- Executive Summary (2-3 paragraphs synthesizing all findings)
- Timeline of Key Events (chronological list from all sources)
- Profiles of Pioneers (one paragraph each with cross-references)
- Comparison Table: General vs. Local Anesthesia (key facts side by side)
- Key Anesthetic Substances (ether, chloroform, nitrous oxide) with historical significance and risks
- Modern Developments snapshot
- Source Consistency Notes (any discrepancies found in cross-validation)

All information must come exclusively from Wikipedia articles retrieved through the tools.

search_wikipedia('history of anesthesia') → identifies article title → get_article('Anesthesia') → get_sections('Anesthesia') → summarize_article_section('Anesthesia', 'History') → extract_key_facts('Anesthesia', 'pioneers and key figures in anesthesia')

The key facts from Chain 1 determine WHICH people to investigate. For each of 3 pioneers:

task_description:
You are a historical science researcher compiling a comparative report on the 1908 Tunguska event, its early scientific investigations, and how it compares to more recent atmospheric impact events. Execute the following research workflow strictly using the provided Wikipedia tools: 

1. Use 'search_wikipedia' with the query 'Tunguska event' to find the exact article title. 
2. Use 'get_sections' on the main article to retrieve its structural outline. 
3. Identify the section that covers the early expeditions to the site (look for titles like 'Expeditions' or 'Early investigations'). Use 'summarize_article_section' on this specific section with a max_length of 250 to discover the name of the Russian mineralogist who led the first Soviet expedition to the impact site in the 1920s. 
4. Once you have identified this scientist (Leonid Kulik), use 'get_summary' on his specific Wikipedia article to determine the exact year he finally reached the Tunguska site and his initial hypothesis regarding why there was no visible impact crater.

6. Use 'get_related_topics' on the 'Tunguska event' article with a limit of 15. Analyze the returned links to identify the article for the famous 21st-century atmospheric meteor explosion that also occurred in Russia (the 2013 Chelyabinsk meteor). 
7. Use 'summarize_article_for_query' on this 21st-century meteor's article with the query 'estimated energy yield in kilotons or megatons of TNT and total number of injuries' (max_length: 200). 
8. Synthesize your findings into a final structured report containing: 
   A) Early Investigation: The name of the first expedition leader, the year he reached the site, and his hypothesis for the missing crater. 
   B) Tunguska Scale: The 5 extracted key facts regarding Tunguska's blast size and energy yield. 
   C) Modern Comparison: The name of the 21st-century Russian meteor event, its estimated energy yield, its reported injuries, and a brief comparison of its explosive yield to the Tunguska event based on the gathered data.

task_description:
You are tasked with compiling a deep-dive historical research report for a presentation in the upcoming week regarding the global and cultural aftermath of the 1815 eruption of Mount Tambora. You must navigate a strict chain of dependencies using the available Wikipedia tools:

1. Phase 1: The Physical Eruption
- Use `Wikipedia:search_wikipedia` for '1815 eruption of Mount Tambora' to identify the exact main article title.
- Using the exact title, use the `Wikipedia:extract_key_facts` tool with the topic 'global climate anomalies and volcanic winter' and set the count to 5 to extract specific scientific impacts.

2. Phase 2: The Climate Anomaly
- Use the `Wikipedia:get_related_topics` tool on the Tambora eruption article. From the results, identify the specific Wikipedia article dedicated to the severe global climate abnormality that occurred the following year (commonly known as the 'Year Without a Summer').
- Use the `Wikipedia:get_sections` tool on this climate anomaly article to map its internal structure.
- Identify the exact section titles that cover the regional impacts in 'Europe' and 'North America'.
- Use the `Wikipedia:summarize_article_section` tool twice to summarize the content of both the European and North American sections (set max_length to 200 for each).

3. Phase 3: The Cultural Impact
- The gloomy weather of that year famously influenced literature. Use the `Wikipedia:get_links` tool on the climate anomaly article to find the link for the specific Swiss mansion/villa near Lake Geneva where Mary Shelley and Lord Byron stayed. (Decision point: if the target link is buried among hundreds of unrelated links, you must synthesize the context to form a fallback query using `Wikipedia:search_wikipedia` such as 'mansion Lake Geneva Mary Shelley 1816' to find the exact article title).
- Use the `Wikipedia:get_article` tool to fetch the full text of the villa's article. Analyze the raw text to extract the names of all the notable literary figures who were present during that specific summer.
- Determine the title of the famous sci-fi/horror novel authored by Mary Shelley that originated during this stay. Use `Wikipedia:search_wikipedia` to find its exact Wikipedia article title.
- Use the `Wikipedia:summarize_article_for_query` tool on the novel's article with the query: 'How did the volcanic winter and dreary weather at the villa influence the writing and conception of this book?' (set max_length to 250).

4. Phase 4: Synthesis
- Combine all gathered information into a final structured Markdown report titled 'The Tambora Aftermath: Climate and Culture'. Your report must include the 5 extracted scientific facts, the regional climate summaries, the list of guests at the villa, and the contextual summary of the novel's conception.
dependency_analysis:
This task enforces a 4-level deep sequential dependency chain with conditional branching, requiring 8 distinct Wikipedia tools.
1. Initial Search -> Title 1: `Wikipedia:search_wikipedia` locates the precise Tambora article title.
2. Title 1 -> Facts & Related Topics: `Wikipedia:extract_key_facts` extracts parameters directly from Title 1, while `Wikipedia:get_related_topics` acts as a required bridging tool to discover Title 2 ('Year Without a Summer').
3. Title 2 -> Sections -> Summaries: `Wikipedia:get_sections` maps Title 2's structure, outputting specific section headers. These dynamically retrieved headers become mandatory input parameters for `Wikipedia:summarize_article_section` to extract targeted regional data.
4. Title 2 -> Links -> Title 3: `Wikipedia:get_links` serves as a discovery mechanism to find Title 3 ('Villa Diodati'). This introduces a conditional decision point: if parsing thousands of links is inefficient, the agent must synthesize context to fallback to `Wikipedia:search_wikipedia`.
5. Title 3 -> Full Text Analysis: `Wikipedia:get_article` fetches raw content, requiring the agent to perform internal data extraction (identifying specific literary guests) rather than relying on a summarization tool.
6. Synthesis -> Title 4 -> Query Summarization: Identifying the authors leads to searching for Title 4 ('Frankenstein'). Finally, `Wikipedia:summarize_article_for_query` synthesizes the cross-article theme by evaluating how the climate event detailed in Title 2 affected the cultural artifact in Title 4.
Data flows sequentially from the physical event -> climate event -> location -> specific cultural artifact, requiring outputs from one tool to strictly become inputs for the next stage.

task_description:
You are a biomedical science historian compiling a comprehensive research briefing on Bioluminescence and the scientific revolution of Green Fluorescent Protein (GFP). Execute the following sequential research workflow using the Wikipedia tools:

Phase 1: General Bioluminescence & Evolution
1. Search for 'Bioluminescence' to determine the exact Wikipedia article title.
2. Extract exactly 3 key facts from this article focusing strictly on the topic 'independent evolution' (to determine how many times this trait evolved independently in nature).
3. Retrieve the sections of the 'Bioluminescence' article. Identify the section title that covers biotechnology, uses, or biomedical applications.
4. Generate a summary of that specific application-focused section (max 150 words).

Phase 2: The GFP Revolution
5. Search for the 'Green fluorescent protein' article.
6. Extract 5 key facts from the GFP article focused on the topic '2008 Nobel Prize in Chemistry' to identify the exact names of the three scientists who shared the award.
7. For each of the three identified Nobel laureates, use the targeted query summary tool on their individual Wikipedia articles with the query: 'specific contribution to the discovery and development of green fluorescent protein' (max length 200).

Phase 3: Ecological Diversity
8. Retrieve related topics for the 'Bioluminescence' article (limit to 15).
9. From the returned related topics, select exactly three specific living bioluminescent organisms (e.g., a specific genus or species, such as a type of bacteria, dinoflagellate, or insect). Do not choose broad chemical terms or non-organism topics.
10. For each of the three selected organisms, generate a targeted summary with the query: 'what is the ecological purpose or function of bioluminescence for this organism?'

Phase 4: Synthesis
Output your final results as a structured JSON object containing:
- 'evolution_count': A string summarizing how many times bioluminescence independently evolved.
- 'biotech_applications': The summary of the applications section.
- 'nobel_laureates': A list of three objects, each containing the laureate's 'name' and their specific 'contribution' (synthesized from Phase 2).

dependency_analysis: This task requires deep, multi-layered tool dependency chains and conditional execution. Chain 1 (Section Targeting): search_wikipedia ('Bioluminescence') -> get_sections (returns list of headings) -> Agent must apply decision logic to identify the correct heading related to 'biotechnology/applications' -> summarize_article_section (uses the exact heading). Chain 2 (Entity Extraction & Iterative Deep Dive): search_wikipedia ('Green fluorescent protein') -> extract_key_facts (parameterized with topic '2008 Nobel Prize') -> Agent extracts three distinct human names from the unstructured text -> Agent executes summarize_article_for_query three separate times (once for each dynamically discovered laureate name). Chain 3 (Topic Discovery & Filtering): get_related_topics ('Bioluminescence') -> Agent evaluates the list to filter out non-organisms -> summarize_article_for_query executed iteratively for the 3 selected organisms. The entire workflow relies on exact title matches passed from tool to tool, forcing the agent to rely exclusively on tool outputs rather than internal knowledge, and demonstrating parallel task execution (the 3 laureates and 3 organisms) stemming from a single origin point.

task_description:

**PHASE 1: Primary Article Mapping**
1. Search Wikipedia for 'Dust Bowl' to identify the main article
2. Retrieve the full article sections to understand the content structure
3. Extract at least 8 key facts from the main article, specifically focused on environmental causes
4. Get all related topics from the Dust Bowl article to identify connected subjects
5. Retrieve all links within the Dust Bowl article

**PHASE 2: Connected Subject Deep Dive**
From the related topics and links discovered in Phase 1, you must investigate at least 4 of the following (select the most historically significant ones based on your findings):
- Government response programs (such as New Deal agencies)
- Key geographic regions affected
- Notable cultural works or documentation
- Migration patterns and destinations

For each selected subject:

2. Get the article sections
3. Summarize at least 2 key sections relevant to the Dust Bowl connection
4. Extract 5 key facts from each

**PHASE 3: Cross-Reference Analysis**

2. For at least 2 such programs, summarize the article for the query: 'What specific actions did this program take to address soil erosion and farmer relief?'
3. Extract key facts about the long-term impact of these programs

**PHASE 4: Comparative Synthesis**
1. Using the 'summarize_article_for_query' tool, query the Dust Bowl article for: 'What lessons about environmental management emerged from this catastrophe?'
2. Get related topics from one of the New Deal program articles you investigated
3. If any modern environmental or agricultural agencies appear in those related topics, search for them and extract 3 key facts about their current approaches to soil conservation

**PHASE 5: Final Report Requirements**
Compile all findings into a structured report containing:

- Government programs and their specific interventions (at least 4 programs)
- Migration statistics and primary destination regions
- Cultural impact summary including at least 3 specific works or figures
- Modern environmental management principles derived from Dust Bowl lessons
- Cross-referenced connections between at least 6 different Wikipedia articles

The final report must demonstrate evidence of information cross-validation between multiple articles and show how facts from one article contextualize findings from another.

2. get_related_topics → search_wikipedia (for connected subjects) → get_article → summarize_article_section

- Government program impacts must be cross-referenced between program articles and Dust Bowl article

1) Title discovery (search_wikipedia):

dependency_analysis:
Available tools are all on the Wikipedia server. We design a multi-stage, multi-branch workflow that consumes and produces data across the tools, requiring careful orchestration and multiple tool calls per city.

Key tool chains and data flow:
- Discovery chain: search_wikipedia → canonical title selection → get_sections → choose section targets.
- Section-driven summarization: get_sections output determines which summarize_article_section calls to make for each topic (Effectiveness, Operation/Charges, Exemptions, Enforcement, Air quality, Criticism). The presence/absence of sections is a critical decision that gates the next tool.
- Fallback summarization: If key sections are absent, the agent must switch to summarize_article_for_query with targeted queries (impact/results, exemptions/equity, charges/operation). Thus, get_sections directly influences parameters for summarize_article_for_query.
- Context and overview: get_summary is used in parallel with section summaries to provide a baseline overview; its output is integrated with targeted summaries and key facts.
- Fact extraction loop: extract_key_facts is run with a primary topic string. If crucial facts (fees, start date) are missing, the agent iteratively re-runs extract_key_facts with an alternative topic string. If still missing, it must fall back to data from summarize_article_section (Operation/Charges) outputs. This constitutes an iterative dependency loop and a multi-branch fallback.
- Related topic expansion: get_related_topics provides a list of candidate pages. Titles matching keywords trigger get_article followed by summarize_article_for_query to harvest outcomes/acceptance/air quality metrics not fully covered in the primary page. This is a scenario-based dependency where related topic titles determine additional tool calls and their query parameters.
- Links-based context: get_links from the primary article is used to detect broader topic pages (e.g., Road pricing). If present, it triggers get_article and summarize_article_for_query to gather background and global comparison context. This creates a parallel enrichment path complementary to get_related_topics.
- Full-text verification: get_article on the primary page is used to cross-check numeric details (dates, fees, percentages) found via summarize_article_section and extract_key_facts. This step validates or contradicts earlier findings, and discrepancies must be recorded.

Critical decision points:
- Title selection from search_wikipedia results: choose the canonical article based on best match.
- Section presence test via get_sections: if an Effectiveness/Impact-type section exists, use summarize_article_section; else pivot to summarize_article_for_query for impact metrics.
- Missing key facts after extract_key_facts: re-run with adjusted topic; if still missing, extract from relevant section summaries; if still unavailable, mark as not specified.
- Related topic selection: from get_related_topics output, pick up to two titles by keyword match (referendum, air quality, public opinion, traffic/emissions). If none match, skip.
- Links-based context: only if get_links contains general context topics (Road pricing/Congestion pricing/Transport in [city]) do we fetch and summarize them.
- Cross-check discrepancies: if full text contradicts section summaries or key facts (e.g., differing fee amounts or start years), record the conflict.

Parallel vs sequential requirements:
- Sequential within a city: search_wikipedia → get_sections → (summarize_article_section and/or summarize_article_for_query) → get_summary → extract_key_facts (and possible re-run) → get_related_topics (and follow-up get_article + summarize_article_for_query) → get_links (and follow-up get_article + summarize_article_for_query if applicable) → get_article (full text) → synthesis and red-flag assessment.
- Parallel across cities: after canonical titles are identified, the same sequence can be executed for London, Stockholm, and Singapore in parallel. Within each city, flows remain ordered due to dependencies.

Cross-server considerations:
- Only the Wikipedia server is available; therefore, all dependencies are intra-server. However, the workflow simulates cross-validation by using different tools within the same server (sections vs summaries vs key facts vs full-text) and by leveraging related topics and intra-article links to triangulate metrics.

Rationale for complexity:
- The task forces the use of every available tool: search_wikipedia (title discovery), get_sections (section map), summarize_article_section (targeted section summaries), summarize_article_for_query (fallbacks and targeted queries), get_summary (overview), extract_key_facts (structured fact harvesting with iterative re-run), get_related_topics (expansion to referendum/air quality/public opinion pages), get_links (discovery of broader context pages), get_article (full-text verification and analysis).
- Multiple decision branches and iterative loops are required (section presence, missing facts, related-topic filtering, links-based enrichment, discrepancy handling).
- The final synthesis requires cross-validation and explicit red-flag rules derived from the extracted content.

INHERENT DEPENDENCIES
- Search → Fetch: Wikipedia:search_wikipedia is used to resolve or confirm canonical page titles, which are then consumed by Wikipedia:get_summary, Wikipedia:get_sections, Wikipedia:summarize_article_section, Wikipedia:summarize_article_for_query, Wikipedia:extract_key_facts, Wikipedia:get_links, and Wikipedia:get_related_topics.
- Sections → Section summaries: Wikipedia:get_sections provides section_title strings required by Wikipedia:summarize_article_section. If suitable sections are not present, Wikipedia:summarize_article_for_query becomes the fallback.
- Title-centric analysis: Wikipedia:get_links and Wikipedia:get_related_topics naturally depend on the selected article title and produce lists of candidate titles for further calls to Wikipedia:get_summary.

SCENARIO-BASED DEPENDENCIES
- Canonical title resolution: Output from Wikipedia:search_wikipedia determines the canonical title T for each technology. All subsequent calls for that technology depend on T.
- Conditional economics and environment summaries: The existence and names of sections from Wikipedia:get_sections dictate whether to use Wikipedia:summarize_article_section or fall back to Wikipedia:summarize_article_for_query with specific queries and max_length values.
- Capacity factor facts-first strategy: Wikipedia:extract_key_facts (topic_within_article="capacity factor") is attempted first. If the returned fact count is less than 2, the flow conditionally triggers Wikipedia:summarize_article_for_query to cover capacity factor content.
- Policy link aggregation and fallback: Wikipedia:get_links (for each T) feeds a keyword filter to build a global set of policy-related titles. If the set size is <3, the workflow conditionally calls Wikipedia:get_related_topics (for each T) to harvest additional titles, which then trigger Wikipedia:get_summary calls for up to 3 selected policy topics.
- Cross-topic intersection: Wikipedia:get_related_topics for each T produces three sets whose intersection I determines whether to deepen on shared topics. If I is non-empty, those intersecting titles are summarized via Wikipedia:get_summary. If I is empty, Wikipedia:search_wikipedia("Renewable energy") is called to find a fallback umbrella article R, which is then consumed by Wikipedia:get_summary and Wikipedia:get_article.
- Deep-dive section selection: For the shared topic S (or fallback R), Wikipedia:get_sections determines whether Wikipedia:summarize_article_section can be used to summarize a policy/economics section; otherwise, Wikipedia:summarize_article_for_query provides a query-focused summary.

CRITICAL DECISION POINTS
- Title selection decision: Choosing the canonical title from search results governs all downstream calls.
- Section presence decisions (economics and environment): If matching sections exist, summarize those; else switch to query-based summaries.
- Capacity factor fact sufficiency: If fewer than 2 facts are extracted, trigger query-based summarization for capacity factors.
- Policy topic sufficiency: If fewer than 3 policy-related link titles are found across all three technologies, expand to related topics and repeat filtering.
- Shared topic presence: If intersection across related topics is empty, fall back to a searched umbrella topic.

PARALLEL VS SEQUENTIAL REQUIREMENTS
- Per-technology pipelines (steps 2–5): Within each technology, calls are sequential due to dependencies (title resolution → sections → section-based or query-based summaries → fact extraction). Across the three technologies, those pipelines may run in parallel.
- Aggregation steps (steps 6–8): These require prior outputs from all three per-technology pipelines (links and related topics) and are therefore sequential and aggregative.

CROSS-SERVER DEPENDENCIES
- Not applicable: Only the Wikipedia server is available. All dependencies and cross-validation are intra-server. The design still enforces cross-article cross-validation within Wikipedia by intersecting related topics and aggregating policy-linked topics.

DATA FLOW SUMMARY
1) search_wikipedia(query=tech) → select canonical title T.
2) get_summary(T), get_sections(T).
3) If matching economics/cost section exists → summarize_article_section(T, section); else → summarize_article_for_query(T, economics query).
4) If matching environmental section exists → summarize_article_section(T, section); else → summarize_article_for_query(T, environment query).
5) extract_key_facts(T, "capacity factor"); if <2 facts → summarize_article_for_query(T, capacity factor query).
6) get_links(T) → filter titles by policy keywords → aggregate; if <3 total → get_related_topics(T) → filter → aggregate; then get_summary for up to 3 selected policy titles.
7) get_related_topics(T) for each technology → compute intersection; if non-empty → get_summary(intersecting titles); else → search_wikipedia("Renewable energy") → get_summary(R), get_article(R).
8) get_sections(S or R) → if policy/economics section exists → summarize_article_section(S/R, section); else → summarize_article_for_query(S/R, policy frameworks query).
These chains enforce that each decision and call relies on prior tool outputs and that multiple branches and fallbacks are used to ensure completeness.

Inherent and scenario-based tool dependencies:

A) Inherent tool chains and data flow:
- Discovery → Retrieval → Structure → Summarization → Fact extraction:
  1) Wikipedia:search_wikipedia identifies candidate article titles for core concepts (e.g., Ukiyo-e, Nishiki-e, Woodblock printing). This search result list directly determines which titles to pass to Wikipedia:get_article.
  2) Wikipedia:get_article retrieves full pages for deep analysis and enables downstream structural queries.
  3) Wikipedia:get_sections exposes the internal section taxonomy (e.g., Technique, Production), which is a prerequisite for Wikipedia:summarize_article_section. If sections exist, the agent can pull focused content; if not, it must pivot to Wikipedia:summarize_article_for_query.
  4) Wikipedia:summarize_article_section yields targeted content when a section is confirmed present; otherwise Wikipedia:summarize_article_for_query tailors the extraction to specific information needs (e.g., production steps, censorship impacts).
  5) Wikipedia:get_summary provides concise overviews for series pages, complementary to the deeper content and useful for quick annotation.
  6) Wikipedia:extract_key_facts structures discrete facts (e.g., technique terms, series highlights), which feed the glossary and series comparisons.
  7) Wikipedia:get_links lists outbound references from artist pages, enabling link-driven verification of series titles and targeted retrieval of their pages.
  8) Wikipedia:get_related_topics surfaces concept adjacency for context building (e.g., Tenpō reforms, censorship) and supports cross-topic triangulation.

B) Scenario-based dependencies and decision points:
- Decision A (Ukiyo-e technique): Use get_sections to check for Technique/Production/Process. If present, summarize that section; else require summarize_article_for_query with technique-focused query. This enforces a dependence on structural discovery before content extraction.
- Decision B (Nishiki-e/Woodblock printing techniques): Identical structural dependence as Decision A, ensuring fallback via summarize_article_for_query if sections are absent.
- Iterative threshold Decision C: After extracting technique facts from Ukiyo-e, Nishiki-e, and Woodblock printing, if fewer than 8 distinct technique terms are available, the workflow requires calling get_links on Ukiyo-e and Nishiki-e to discover additional technique-related pages. Then summaries of those linked pages supplement the glossary. This sets up a conditional loop where insufficient coverage triggers additional exploration and aggregation.
- Decision D (Artists Hokusai/Hiroshige): Section-dependent extraction prioritizes Works/Notable works/Artistic style; if none are present, summarize_for_query targets notable series and stylistic themes. The subsequent use of get_links validates and discovers specified series titles. If a series is not discoverable via links, the agent must directly fetch it via get_article, then summarize and extract facts—explicitly chaining link presence to retrieval choices.
- Decision E (Tenpō reforms context): Section-targeted extraction is attempted first; if missing, summarize_for_query is required with specific cultural impact tokens. Additionally, a dependent search for "Censorship in the Edo period" determines whether to use that exact page or the closest censorship-related result discovered by search. Cross-validation then depends on summarize_article_for_query for "Ukiyo-e" to confirm or contrast impacts across articles.
- Cross-validation dependency: Statements about censorship and sumptuary laws must be corroborated between the Tenpō reforms page, the censorship-in-Edo page, and targeted summaries from the Ukiyo-e page. Contradictions must be recorded, requiring multi-article synthesis.

C) Parallel vs sequential requirements:
- Sequential: Core concept establishment (search → get_article → get_sections → summarize) must precede technique aggregation and glossary construction, because the iterative threshold is evaluated on that aggregate.
- Parallelizable components: Artist-specific processing for Hokusai and Hiroshige can occur in parallel once the technique foundation is set; each artist follows the same chain (get_article → get_sections → conditional summarize → get_links → series retrieval with summaries and key facts).
- Context integration must follow after core technique and artist data is available, to enable meaningful cross-validation in light of Tenpō reforms and censorship topics.

D) Data transformation and conditional workflows:
- The agent must transform extracted text into structured sections (workflow steps, glossary terms, series comparisons, timeline bullets) with exact counts. The technique term aggregation requires deduplication across multiple extract_key_facts outputs. The iterative threshold enforces a conditional expansion using links if the minimum of 8 terms is not met.
- The series confirmation uses link presence as a decision node; absent links trigger direct article retrieval, ensuring robust completion.

E) Server considerations:
- All tools operate on the Wikipedia server; there are no cross-server calls available in this environment. Cross-validation is achieved by combining multiple Wikipedia articles and tools rather than multi-server sources.

Overall, the task requires understanding that: (1) get_sections must condition the choice between summarize_article_section and summarize_article_for_query; (2) link discovery via get_links determines whether to fetch series pages directly or via fallback; (3) extract_key_facts aggregation across multiple sources enables threshold-based iteration; and (4) cross-topic validation depends on coordinating summarize_article_for_query across multiple articles. task_description:
Create a comprehensive research dossier on the Wright Brothers' invention of powered flight, tracing their complete journey from bicycle mechanics to aviation pioneers. Your analysis must:

1. **Background Investigation**: Research the Wright brothers' early life, their bicycle business, and how their mechanical expertise influenced their approach to flight. Extract key facts about their upbringing and careers before aviation.

2. **Technical Innovation Analysis**: Identify and explain the THREE fundamental problems of flight they solved: lift generation, three-axis control, and propulsion. For each problem, document their specific innovations and how they differed from other aviation pioneers' approaches.

3. **Testing Methodology Documentation**: Research their systematic experimentation process, including their wind tunnel tests (how many wing shapes tested?), glider experiments at Kitty Hawk (years and results), and data collection methods.

4. **First Flight Details**: Document the December 17, 1903 achievements - extract specific data on: number of flights that day, distances achieved, durations, wind conditions, and who witnessed the flights.

5. **Competitive Landscape Analysis**: Identify at least FIVE other aviation pioneers working on powered flight in the same era (e.g., Samuel Langley, Glenn Curtiss, Alberto Santos-Dumont, Otto Lilienthal, Octave Chanze). For each, summarize their approach and compare it to the Wrights' method.

6. **Patent and Legal Battles**: Research the Wright brothers' patent strategy and their legal conflicts. Identify the specific patent number and what it covered, plus key litigation outcomes.

7. **Legacy Assessment**: Compile information on museums dedicated to their work, memorial sites, and how historians rank their contribution among the most significant inventions in history.

For each component, you must:
- Start with targeted searches to identify relevant articles
- Extract key facts using fact extraction tools
- Cross-reference information across multiple articles using links and related topics
- Summarize specific sections when detailed information is needed
- Validate facts by checking multiple sources

Final output should be a structured report with each section containing at least 5 specific facts extracted from Wikipedia, properly sourced to the articles from which they came.

task_description:
Research Brief: Reconstruct and cross-validate the sequence, physical phenomena, and global impacts of the 1883 eruption of Krakatoa using Wikipedia tools only. Build a consolidated, discrepancy-aware report by chaining searches, section-targeted summaries, link/related-topic expansions, and key-fact extraction across multiple articles.

Scope and focus:
- Anchor topic: 1883 eruption of Krakatoa (sequence of major events, tsunamis, pressure waves)
- Phenomena: global atmospheric optics (e.g., Bishop's Ring, unusual sunsets), pressure wave/barograph records, climatic effects (volcanic winter), tsunami heights and casualties
- Cross-article validation: compare facts across multiple relevant pages; resolve discrepancies via targeted section summaries

Search queries (run each with limit = 5):
1) "1883 eruption of Krakatoa"
2) "Krakatoa"
3) "Bishop's Ring"
4) "Volcanic winter"
5) "Krakatoa tsunami 1883"
6) "Krakatoa pressure wave barograph"

Relevance criteria for search results:
- Consider an article relevant if its summary contains at least one of the case-insensitive keywords: ["krakatoa", "1883", "eruption", "volcanic", "tsunami", "bishop", "pressure"]. Use Wikipedia:get_summary on each returned title to check.

Core workflow and tool dependencies:
1) Candidate discovery (sequential):
   - Use Wikipedia:search_wikipedia for the six queries above (limit = 5)
   - For all returned titles, call Wikipedia:get_summary
   - Filter to relevant titles per criteria

2) Anchor article confirmation and deep-dive (sequential):
   - Ensure at least two anchors are selected: one titled exactly or closest to "1883 eruption of Krakatoa", and one titled exactly or closest to "Krakatoa" (choose the best-matching titles from search summaries)
   - For each anchor, call Wikipedia:get_sections
   - From the returned section list, select up to 3 sections whose titles contain any of ["Eruption", "Timeline", "Aftermath", "Effects", "Climate", "Tsunami", "Legacy", "Scientific"] (case-insensitive)
   - For each selected section, call Wikipedia:summarize_article_section with max_length = 200 and collect details
   - For each anchor, call Wikipedia:extract_key_facts with topic_within_article set to each of the following and count = 5:
     a) "sequence of eruption events (dates and times)"
     b) "tsunami height and casualties"
     c) "pressure wave barograph observations"
     d) "global atmospheric optical phenomena (Bishop's Ring, sunsets)"
     e) "climatic impact (volcanic winter, temperature anomalies)"
   - If any category returns fewer than 3 key facts for an anchor, call Wikipedia:get_article for that anchor and manually augment the facts using the full content plus additional targeted Wikipedia:summarize_article_section calls based on relevant sections discovered

3) Related-topic expansion (branching):
   - For each anchor, call Wikipedia:get_related_topics with limit = 15
   - If "Volcanic winter" appears among related topics for either anchor, include that article as a third core source; otherwise, fallback: use Wikipedia:search_wikipedia with query "Volcanic winter krakatoa" (limit = 5) and pick the best-matching title via Wikipedia:get_summary
   - If "Bishop's Ring" appears among related topics, include it; otherwise, if not already selected in step 1, perform a fallback search using Wikipedia:search_wikipedia with query "Bishop's Ring Krakatoa" (limit = 5) and pick the best-matching title via Wikipedia:get_summary

4) Link-driven instrumentation deep-dive (conditional):
   - Call Wikipedia:get_links on the chosen anchor titled closest to "1883 eruption of Krakatoa"
   - If any link title contains "barograph" or "barometer" (case-insensitive), select one such title and call Wikipedia:summarize_article_for_query on it with query = "Krakatoa pressure wave observations (circumnavigations, period, amplitude)" and max_length = 250 to capture measurement context

5) Phenomena-focused extraction (parallel):
   - For each of the additional included articles (e.g., "Volcanic winter", "Bishop's Ring"), call Wikipedia:get_sections and select up to 2 sections with titles containing any of ["Effects", "Observations", "History", "Impact", "Phenomena"]
   - Call Wikipedia:summarize_article_section (max_length = 200) for the selected sections
   - Call Wikipedia:extract_key_facts with topic_within_article tuned to the phenomena: for "Volcanic winter": "global temperature change magnitude and duration"; for "Bishop's Ring": "optical characteristics and duration of post-Krakatoa observations"; count = 5 in each case

6) Cross-validation and discrepancy handling (sequential with decision points):
   - Sequence/time of main explosions: Compare the times/dates of the largest eruptive events as reported by the anchors' extracted key facts and any section summaries. If the reported times for the principal explosion differ by >= 30 minutes across sources, flag a discrepancy and provide both (or multiple) reported times with article titles and section references
   - Tsunami height: Compare the maximum tsunami height reported by the anchors and any tsunami-focused article found. If maximum reported heights differ by >= 5 meters, flag a discrepancy and list all values with sources
   - Pressure wave: Consolidate the number of global circumnavigations and typical period/amplitude from anchors and the barograph-related article summary. If conflicting counts of circumnavigations are found, list all counts and sources
   - Climatic impact: Prefer the "Volcanic winter" article for global mean temperature anomaly magnitude and duration. If no numeric magnitude is found there, fallback to anchors' climate/effects sections. If ranges or multiple values are given, present the range and sources

7) Final consolidation and output formatting (sequential):
   - Produce a structured report with the following sections:
     - Consolidated sequence of key events (dates/times as reported; note time standards if mentioned, e.g., local vs UTC)
     - Tsunami heights and casualties (values, sources, and discrepancy flags if any)
     - Pressure wave observations (circumnavigations, period/amplitude, sources, discrepancy flags if any)
     - Global atmospheric optical phenomena (what, where, how long; e.g., Bishop's Ring, sunsets; with sources)
     - Climatic impact (temperature anomaly magnitude/duration with preference/fallback logic; sources and discrepancies)
     - Related topics map: at least 5 related topic titles encountered via Wikipedia:get_related_topics or Wikipedia:get_links and a one-line note on how each informed the analysis (e.g., contributed climate data, optical phenomena context, instrumentation background)
   - Include a "Methodology and Tool Trace" appendix listing:
     - The exact tool calls executed (tool name and target title)
     - Which decision branches were triggered (e.g., volcanic winter fallback, barograph link present or not)
     - Any fallback searches performed and why

Execution constraints and exact parameters:
- Use the exact queries and keyword lists above
- For each article where sections are summarized, select at most 3 sections (anchors) or 2 sections (additional articles) as specified
- Maximize parallelism where possible (e.g., section summaries for multiple articles can be done in parallel), but honor decision points before proceeding to dependent steps
- Discrepancy thresholds are strict: time difference >= 30 minutes; tsunami maximum height difference >= 5 meters
- Ensure at least three core articles are used in-depth: two anchors ("1883 eruption of Krakatoa" and "Krakatoa" or closest matches) and at least one phenomena article ("Volcanic winter" or "Bishop's Ring")
- All information must be sourced from the content returned by the specified Wikipedia tools; do not use any other sources

Inherent dependencies and tool chains:
- Standard discovery chain: Wikipedia:search_wikipedia → Wikipedia:get_summary → (filter) → Wikipedia:get_sections → Wikipedia:summarize_article_section. This leverages search for candidates, summaries for relevance filtering, sections to scope content, and section summaries for targeted extraction.
- Fact extraction synergy: Wikipedia:extract_key_facts complements section summaries to efficiently gather structured facts; when insufficient, Wikipedia:get_article provides full text fallback.
- Topic expansion: Wikipedia:get_related_topics and Wikipedia:get_links broaden scope; their outputs determine additional titles for deeper analysis and tailored summaries via Wikipedia:summarize_article_for_query.

Scenario-based dependencies and decision points:
- Anchor selection depends on search results and summary keyword matching (ensures that subsequent deep-dive targets are appropriate). If exact matches to "1883 eruption of Krakatoa"/"Krakatoa" are not found, closest matching titles are chosen via get_summary content.
- Section selection depends on get_sections output; only sections containing predefined focus keywords are summarized, ensuring content relevance.
- Extract-key-facts sufficiency check: If Wikipedia:extract_key_facts yields fewer than 3 facts for a category in an anchor article, the workflow escalates to Wikipedia:get_article and additional Wikipedia:summarize_article_section calls to manually augment facts (iterative refinement loop).
- Related-topic branch: The presence of "Volcanic winter" or "Bishop's Ring" in Wikipedia:get_related_topics results determines whether to include those articles directly; absence triggers fallback searches via Wikipedia:search_wikipedia with specific queries and subsequent Wikipedia:get_summary validation (conditional workflow).
- Link-driven instrumentation: Wikipedia:get_links on the Krakatoa eruption anchor determines whether to consult instrumentation pages (e.g., "barograph"); if present, Wikipedia:summarize_article_for_query is applied with a focused query to extract pressure-wave measurement context (tool result determines next tool and parameters).
- Cross-validation: Key facts from multiple articles (anchors and phenomena pages) are compared. Detected discrepancies beyond defined thresholds (>= 30 min for event times; >= 5 m for tsunami heights) trigger discrepancy flags and require listing all divergent values with sources. The climatic impact branch prefers data from the "Volcanic winter" article; if absent, it falls back to anchors' climate/effects sections (parameter precedence with fallback).

Parallel vs sequential requirements:
- Discovery and relevance filtering (search + summary) can be done in parallel across queries, but anchor confirmation must be completed before section selection and extraction for those anchors.
- Section summarization and key-fact extraction from multiple chosen articles can proceed in parallel once the article list is finalized.
- Decision-dependent steps (related-topic inclusion, instrumentation deep-dive) are sequential, triggered by outputs of get_related_topics and get_links respectively.

Data flow patterns:
- Titles from search/summaries feed into sections and related topics tools; selected section titles parameterize summarize_article_section calls.
- Related topics and links produce new titles that seed summarize_article_for_query and additional extract_key_facts calls.
- Extracted facts and section summaries are aggregated and compared to enforce discrepancy logic and compile the final report.

Cross-server considerations:
- Only the Wikipedia server is available; thus, all dependencies are intra-server. No cross-server fallbacks are applicable. The design ensures robustness via intra-server fallbacks (e.g., related-topics absence triggers additional Wikipedia searches) and iterative escalation from extract_key_facts to full-article parsing when needed.

1) Seed discovery (establish base article and section map):
   a. Use Wikipedia:search_wikipedia with query="Hanseatic League", limit=3. Select the title that exactly matches or best matches "Hanseatic League".
   b. Use Wikipedia:get_summary on the selected "Hanseatic League" page; capture a 2–3 sentence overview.
   c. Use Wikipedia:get_sections for the same page; record all section titles for decision-making.

2) Section-focused extraction on the base page (adaptive):
   - Target section names (case-insensitive match): ["History", "Origins", "Trade", "Economy", "Members", "Kontors", "Decline", "Conflicts", "Legacy"].

3) Core key facts extraction from the base page:
   - Use Wikipedia:extract_key_facts with title="Hanseatic League", topic_within_article="founding; peak period; decline; dissolution; trade goods; kontors; treaties", count=7. Store the facts.
   - Decision: If fewer than 5 facts are returned, then use Wikipedia:get_article (full content) followed by Wikipedia:summarize_article_for_query on the same page with query="founding date, peak era, dissolution year, major trade goods, major Kontors, key treaties" (max_length=250) to augment the facts list.

From the returned titles, check for presence of any of the following (exact or closely matching known kontor/city pages): Novgorod (or a kontor page commonly called "Peterhof"), Bergen (or "Bryggen"), Bruges, London (or "Steelyard (London)").

     • Wikipedia:search_wikipedia query="Steelyard (London)", limit=5
     • Wikipedia:search_wikipedia query="Bryggen", limit=5
     • Wikipedia:search_wikipedia query="Bruges Hanseatic", limit=5
     • Wikipedia:search_wikipedia query="Hanseatic Kontor Novgorod Peterhof", limit=5
     Add any matched titles to reach up to 4 kontor/city targets total.

5) Kontor/city deep dives (parallelizable across selected targets): For each selected kontor/city page (up to 4):
   a. Use Wikipedia:get_article to retrieve full content of the specific kontor/city page.
   b. Use Wikipedia:get_sections on that page and look for these section titles: ["History", "Trade", "Economy", "Organization", "Relations with locals", "Decline"]. For each present, use Wikipedia:summarize_article_section with max_length=180.

Select the best matching list/article, run Wikipedia:get_summary, then Wikipedia:get_sections to locate a section that enumerates cities (e.g., "Cities", "Members"), and use Wikipedia:summarize_article_section with max_length=180.

   - Conflicts/treaties: Provide 3–5 bullets summarizing counterparties and outcomes, citing insights from step 7 summaries.
   - Member cities: Provide an alphabetical list of 10 notable member cities identified from the membership content (steps 2 and/or 8). If more than 10 are available, choose those most frequently mentioned across the base and kontor pages.
   - Network mapping: Present the adjacency lists defined in step 9.

Strict rules and constraints:
- Use only the specified Wikipedia tools. Do not reference or rely on any source outside these tool outputs.
- Follow all decision points and fallbacks exactly as described. Implement thresholds as given (e.g., goods >=5, kontor targets >=3, key facts >=5, etc.).
- Use the following exact parameters for tool calls where specified (limits, max_length, counts). When not specified, use defaults.
